2019.explanation_text: For a 12 kW, 0.6 pf lagging load, [latex]\begin{aligned} P_L &= 12kW\\ Q_L&= \frac{12}{0.6} \times \sin (cos^{-1} 0.6)\\ &= 16kVAR \end{aligned} [/latex] Trasformer rating , S=25kVA Let us assume load thet can be added is P kW then, [latex]\begin{aligned} S^2 &=(P+P_L)^2+Q_L^2 \\ 25^2&= (P+12)^2+16^2\\ P &= 7.21kW \end{aligned}[/latex]
2019.explanation_html:
For a 12 kW, 0.6 pf lagging load,
[latex]\begin{aligned} P_L &= 12kW\\ Q_L&= \frac{12}{0.6} \times \sin (cos^{-1} 0.6)\\ &= 16kVAR \end{aligned} [/latex]
Trasformer rating , S=25kVA
Let us assume load thet can be added is P kW then,
[latex]\begin{aligned} S^2 &=(P+P_L)^2+Q_L^2 \\ 25^2&= (P+12)^2+16^2\\ P &= 7.21kW \end{aligned}[/latex]

2019.text: A 220 V DC shunt motor takes 3 A at no-load. It draws 25 A when running at full-load at 1500 rpm. The armature and shunt resistances are 0.5 [latex]\Omega[/latex] and 220 [latex]\Omega[/latex],respectively. The no-load speed in rpm (round off to two decimal places) is ________
2019.html: A 220 V DC shunt motor takes 3 A at no-load. It draws 25 A when running at full-load at 1500 rpm. The armature and shunt resistances are 0.5 [latex]\Omega[/latex] and 220 [latex]\Omega[/latex],respectively. The no-load speed in rpm (round off to two decimal places) is ________
2019.subject: Electrical Machines - DC Machines
2019.explanation_text:
[latex]\begin{aligned}
&\text{At full load condition,}\\
 N_1&=1500 \; \text{rpm} \\ 
I_1 &=25A \\ 
 I_f&= \frac{220V}{200\Omega }=1A\\ 
 I_{a1}&=I_1-I_f=24A \\ 
 E_{g1}&=V-I_{a1}R_a \\ 
 &=220-24 \times 0.5=208V \\ 
&\text{At no-load condition,}\\
 I_2&= 3A\\ 
 I_f&= 1A\\ 
I_{a2}&=I_2-I_f=2A \\ 
 E_{g2}&=220-2 \times 0.5=219V \\ 
 E_g&\propto \phi N \\ 
& \text{Flux id constant,}\\
 E_g&\propto N \\ 
 \frac{E_{g2}}{E_{g1}}&=\frac{N_2}{N_1} \\ 
 \frac{219}{208}&=\frac{N_2}{1500} \\ 
 N_2&= 1579.33 \;\text{rpm}
\end{aligned}[/latex]
2019.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} &\text{At full load condition,}\\ N_1&=1500 \; \text{rpm} \\ I_1 &=25A \\ I_f&= \frac{220V}{200\Omega }=1A\\ I_{a1}&=I_1-I_f=24A \\ E_{g1}&=V-I_{a1}R_a \\ &=220-24 \times 0.5=208V \\ &\text{At no-load condition,}\\ I_2&= 3A\\ I_f&= 1A\\ I_{a2}&=I_2-I_f=2A \\ E_{g2}&=220-2 \times 0.5=219V \\ E_g&\propto \phi N \\ & \text{Flux id constant,}\\ E_g&\propto N \\ \frac{E_{g2}}{E_{g1}}&=\frac{N_2}{N_1} \\ \frac{219}{208}&=\frac{N_2}{1500} \\ N_2&= 1579.33 \;\text{rpm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

2019.text: A delta-connected, 3.7 kW, 400 V(line), three-phase, 4-pole, 50-Hz squirrel-cage induction motor  has  the  following  equivalent circuit  parameters  per  phase  referred  to  the  stator: [latex]R_1=5.39\Omega,R_2=5.72\Omega,X_1=X_2=8.22\Omega[/latex]. Neglect  shunt  branch  in  the  equivalent circuit. 2019.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} I_L &=\sqrt{3}I_{ph} \\ \text{At} \;\; f &= 10Hz, \\ X_1=X_2 &=8.22 \times \frac{10}{50}=1.644\Omega \\ I_{ph} &= \frac{V_{ph}}{\sqrt{(R_1+R_2)^2+(X_1+X_2)^2}} \\ &=\frac{100}{\sqrt{(5.39+5.72)^2+(1.644+1.644)^2}} \\ &= \frac{100}{11.586}=8.63\\ I_L&= 14.95A \end{aligned}[/latex]

2019.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} V_s&= 400kV\\ l&=300km\\ L_1&=1mH/km/phase\\ C_1&=0.01 \mu F/km/phase\\ v&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{L_1C_1}}\\ &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.01 \times 10^{-6}}}\\ &=3.16 \times 10^5 km/sec\\ \beta '&=\frac{2 \pi f l}{v}\\ &=\frac{2 \pi \times 50 \times 300}{3.16 \times 10^5}=0.29\\ A&=1-\frac{\beta ^2}{2}\\ &=1-\frac{(0.29)^2}{2}=0.955\\ V_R&=\frac{V_S}{A}=\frac{400}{0.955}=418.85kV \end{aligned}[/latex]

2019.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} X_1&=0.25 \; p.u.\\ X_2&=0.15 \; p.u.\\ X_0&=0.05 \; p.u.\\ I_{f(LG)}&=I_{f(3-\phi )}\\ \frac{3V_{pu}}{(X_1+X_2+X_0+3X_n)}&=\frac{V_{pu}}{X_1}\\ \frac{3 \times 1}{(0.25+0.15+0.05+3X_n)}&=\frac{1}{0.25}\\ \frac{3}{0.46+3X_n}&=\frac{1}{0.25}\\ \Rightarrow \;\; X_n&=0.1\; p.u.\\ X_n&=0.1 \times Z_B\\ &=0.1 \times \frac{30^2}{50}\\ &=1.8\Omega \end{aligned}[/latex]

2019.text: In  a  DC-DC  boost  converter, the  duty  ratio  is  controlled  to  regulate  the  output  voltage at 48 V. The input DC voltage is 24 V. The output power is 120 W. 2019.html: In a DC-DC boost converter, the duty ratio is controlled to regulate the output voltage at 48 V. The input DC voltage is 24 V. The output power is 120 W. The switching frequency is 50 kHz. Assume ideal components and a very large output filter capacitor. The converter operates at the boundary between continuous and discontinuous conduction modes. The value of the boost inductor (in [latex]\mu H[/latex]) is _______.
2019.subject: Power Electronics - Choppers
2019.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} P_0&=120W,\\ V_s&=24V\\ V_0&=48V\\ V_0&=\frac{V_s}{(1-D)}\\ 1-D&=\frac{24}{48}\\ D&=0.5\\ P_0&=V_0I_0=120\\ I_0&=\frac{120}{48}=2.54A\\ V_sI_s&=V_0I_0\\ I_s&=\frac{120}{24}=5A \end{aligned}[/latex] At boundary of continuous and discontinuous, [latex]\begin{aligned} I_L&=I_s=\frac{\Delta I_{L}}{2}\\ \Delta I_L&=\frac{DV_s}{fL_c}=2 \times 5\\ L_c&=\frac{0.5 \times 24}{50 \times 10^3 \times 10}=24\mu H \end{aligned}[/latex]
2019.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} P_0&=120W,\\ V_s&=24V\\ V_0&=48V\\ V_0&=\frac{V_s}{(1-D)}\\ 1-D&=\frac{24}{48}\\ D&=0.5\\ P_0&=V_0I_0=120\\ I_0&=\frac{120}{48}=2.54A\\ V_sI_s&=V_0I_0\\ I_s&=\frac{120}{24}=5A \end{aligned}[/latex]
At boundary of continuous and discontinuous,
[latex]\begin{aligned} I_L&=I_s=\frac{\Delta I_{L}}{2}\\ \Delta I_L&=\frac{DV_s}{fL_c}=2 \times 5\\ L_c&=\frac{0.5 \times 24}{50 \times 10^3 \times 10}=24\mu H \end{aligned}[/latex]

point (2,-1,1) in the direction of the vector [latex]p=i+ 2j + 2k[/latex] is
2018.html: The value of the directional derivative of the function [latex]\phi (x,y,z)=xy^{2}+yz^{2}+zx^{2}[/latex] at the point (2,-1,1) in the direction of the vector [latex]p=i+ 2j + 2k[/latex] is
2018.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
2018.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} \phi &= xy^2+yz^2+zx^2\\ \bigtriangledown \phi &=\bar{i}\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial x}+\bar{j}\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial y} +\bar{k}\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial z} \\ &=\bar{i}(y^2+2xz)+\bar{j}(2xy+z^2)\\&+\bar{k}(2yz+x^2) \\ \bigtriangledown \phi _{(2,-1,1)} &= \bar{i}(1+4)+\bar{j}(-4+1)+\bar{k}(-2+4)\\ &= 5\bar{i}-3\bar{j}+2\bar{k}\\ \bar{P} &= \bar{i}+2\bar{j}+2\bar{k}\\ |\bar{P}|&=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3 \end{aligned}[/latex] THe directional derivative of f(x,y,z) at (2,-1,1) in the direction of [latex]\bar{P}[/latex] is [latex]\bigtriangledown \phi _{at \; P} \cdot \frac{\bar{P}}{|\bar{P}|}= (5\bar{i}-3\bar{j}+2\bar{k})\left ( \frac{\bar{i}+2\bar{j}+2\bar{k}}{3} \right )=\frac{5-6+4}{3}=1[/latex]
2018.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \phi &= xy^2+yz^2+zx^2\\ \bigtriangledown \phi &=\bar{i}\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial x}+\bar{j}\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial y} +\bar{k}\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial z} \\ &=\bar{i}(y^2+2xz)+\bar{j}(2xy+z^2)\\&+\bar{k}(2yz+x^2) \\ \bigtriangledown \phi _{(2,-1,1)} &= \bar{i}(1+4)+\bar{j}(-4+1)+\bar{k}(-2+4)\\ &= 5\bar{i}-3\bar{j}+2\bar{k}\\ \bar{P} &= \bar{i}+2\bar{j}+2\bar{k}\\ |\bar{P}|&=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3 \end{aligned}[/latex]
THe directional derivative of f(x,y,z) at (2,-1,1) in the direction of [latex]\bar{P}[/latex] is [latex]\bigtriangledown \phi _{at \; P} \cdot \frac{\bar{P}}{|\bar{P}|}= (5\bar{i}-3\bar{j}+2\bar{k})\left ( \frac{\bar{i}+2\bar{j}+2\bar{k}}{3} \right )=\frac{5-6+4}{3}=1[/latex]

2018.explanation_text: A is 2 x 2 matrix [latex]\begin{aligned} Tr\; A&=4\\ \lambda _1+\lambda _2&=4\\ tr(A^2)&=5\\ \lambda _1^2+\lambda _2^2&=5\\ (\lambda _1+\lambda _2)^2&=\lambda _1^2+\lambda _2^2+2\lambda _1 \lambda _2\\ 2\lambda _1 \lambda _2+5&=16\\ 2\lambda _1 \lambda _2&=11\\ \lambda _1 \lambda _2&=\frac{11}{2}\\ |A|&=\frac{11}{2}=5.5 \end{aligned}[/latex]

2018.html: Let f be a real-valued function of a real variable defined as f (x)=x-[x], where [x] denotes the largest integer less than or equal to x. The value of [latex]\int_{0.25}^{1.25}f(x)dx[/latex] is _______ (up to 2 decimal places).
2018.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
2018.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} \int_{0.25}^{1.25} f(x)dx&=\int_{0.25}^{1}(x-[x])dx+\int_{1}^{1.25}(x-[x])dx \\ &= \int_{0.25}^{1.25}(xdx)-\left [ \int_{0.25}^{1}[x]dx+\int_{1}^{1.25}[x]dx \right ]\\ &=\left.\begin{matrix} \left ( \frac{x^2}{2} \right ) \end{matrix}\right|_{0.25}^{1.25}-\left ( \int_{0.25}^{1}0dx+\int_{1}^{1.25}1dx \right ) \\ &=\frac{(1.25)^2}{2}-\left ( \frac{(0.25)^2}{2} \right )-(0+0.25) \\ &=\frac{1}{2}[(1.5625-0.0625)]-0.25 \\ &= 0.5 \end{aligned}[/latex]

The series impedance matrix of a short three-phase transmission line in phase coordinates
is [latex]\begin{bmatrix} Z_{s} & Z_{m} &Z_{m} \\ Z_{m}& Z_{s}& Z_{m}\\ Z_{m}& Z_{m}& Z_{s} \end{bmatrix}[/latex]. If the positive sequence impedance is [latex](1 + j10)\Omega[/latex], and the zero

2018.html:
The series impedance matrix of a short three-phase transmission line in phase coordinates is
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} Z_{s} & Z_{m} &Z_{m} \\ Z_{m}& Z_{s}& Z_{m}\\ Z_{m}& Z_{m}& Z_{s} \end{bmatrix}[/latex].
If the positive sequence impedance is [latex](1 + j10)\Omega[/latex], and the zero sequence is [latex](4 + j31)\Omega[/latex], then the imaginary part of [latex]Z_{m}[/latex] (in [latex]\Omega[/latex]) is ______(up to 2 decimal places).
2018.subject: Power Systems - Fault Analysis
2018.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} Z_1&=(1+j10)\Omega \\ Z_0&=(4+j31)\Omega \\ \text{we know,}\\ Z_1&=Z_s-Z_m\\ Z_0&=Z_s+2Z_m\\ Z_1-Z_0&=-3Z_m\\ Z_m&=\frac{Z_0-Z_1}{3}\\ &=\frac{4+j31-1-j10}{3}\\ &=\frac{3+j21}{3}\\ &=1+j7 \end{aligned}[/latex] The imaginary part of [latex]Z_m[/latex] is 7.00.
2018.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} Z_1&=(1+j10)\Omega \\ Z_0&=(4+j31)\Omega \\ \text{we know,}\\ Z_1&=Z_s-Z_m\\ Z_0&=Z_s+2Z_m\\ Z_1-Z_0&=-3Z_m\\ Z_m&=\frac{Z_0-Z_1}{3}\\ &=\frac{4+j31-1-j10}{3}\\ &=\frac{3+j21}{3}\\ &=1+j7 \end{aligned}[/latex]
The imaginary part of [latex]Z_m[/latex] is 7.00.

2018.text: A separately excited dc motor has an armature resistance [latex]R_{a}= 0.05\Omega[/latex]. The field excitation is kept constant. At an armature voltage of 100 V, the motor produces a torque of 500 Nm at zero speed. Neglecting all mechanical losses, the no-load speed of the motor (in radian/s) for an armature voltage of 150 V is _____ (up to 2 decimal places).
2018.html: A separately excited dc motor has an armature resistance [latex]R_{a}= 0.05\Omega[/latex]. The field excitation is kept constant. At an armature voltage of 100 V, the motor produces a torque of 500 Nm at zero speed. Neglecting all mechanical losses, the no-load speed of the motor (in radian/s) for an armature voltage of 150 V is _____ (up to 2 decimal places).
2018.subject: Electrical Machines - DC Machines
2018.explanation_text:
Given separately initiated DC motor, Field excitaion is constant, Producing a torque of 500 N-m [latex]\begin{aligned}
&\text{At zero speed,}\\
 \because \; N&= 0,\; E_b=0\\ 
E_b &= V-I_aR_a\\ 
 0&= 100-I_a(0.05)\\ 
\therefore \; I_{a1} &=\frac{100}{0.05} =2000A\\ 
T &= \frac{60}{2 \pi N}E_bI_a\\ 
 &= \frac{60}{2 \pi N}\frac{\phi ZNP}{60A}\cdot I_a\\ 
\text{Let,}\;\; T_1&=\frac{1}{2 \pi}\frac{ZP}{A}\phi I_{a1}\;\text{N-m} \\ 
\text{Let,}\;\; T_1 &=kI_{a1} \\ 
\text{where,}\;\; k &= \frac{1}{2 \pi}\frac{ZP \phi}{A}\\ 
T_1 &= 500 \text{N-m}, \\
I_{a1}&=2000A\\
k&=\frac{500}{2000}=0.25
\end{aligned}[/latex] When motor runs on no-load given all mechanical losses neglected. No-load current is negligible and the voltage drop at no-load can be negligible. [latex]\begin{aligned}
\therefore \;\;E_b &\simeq V=150V \\ 
 E_b&= \frac{\phi ZNP}{60A}\\ 
\text{Already solved,}\\
 k&=\frac{1}{2\pi} \frac{ZP \phi }{A}\\ 
 \therefore \;\;\frac{ZP \phi }{A} &=2 \pi (k) \\ 
 \therefore \;\; E_b &= 2 \pi (k) \cdot \frac{N}{60}\\ 
\therefore \;\; E_b&= k \times \omega \\ 
(\omega : & \text{No-load speed in rad/sec})\\
\therefore \;\;\omega  &= \frac{E_b}{k}\\ 
\therefore \;\;\omega  &= \frac{150}{0.25}\\ 
\omega &= 600 \text{rad/sec}
\end{aligned}[/latex]

2018.html: A transformer with toroidal core of permeability [latex]\mu[/latex] is shown in the figure. Assuming uniform flux density across the circular core cross-section of radius [latex]r\lt \lt R[/latex], and neglecting any leakage flux, the best estimate for the mean radius R is
2018.subject: Electrical Machines - Single Phase Induction Motors, Special Purpose Machines and Electromechanical Energy Conversion System
2018.explanation_text:
Since we know reluctance of core: [latex]\Re =\frac{l_c}{\mu a}[/latex] Here, [latex] l_c= [/latex] mean core length, a= area of core reluctance, [latex]
\begin{aligned}
\Re &=\frac{2 \pi R}{\mu  \times \pi r^2}\\
&=\frac{2R}{\mu r^2}\\
[\text{where} R &= \text{mean radius of core}] \\ 
\text{or}\;\; R&=\frac{\Re \mu r^2}{2} \\ 

\text{and}\;\; \Re &= \frac{mmf}{flux}=\frac{N_pI_p}{\phi }\\ 
\text{Here,}\;\; \phi &=-\frac{1}{N_p}\int_{0}^{t}e\;dt \\ 
[\text{where}\; e &\text{is primary generated voltage}] \\ 
\text{or}\;\;  \phi  &=-\frac{1}{N_p}\int_{0}^{t}-(V_p)\;dt \\ 
 \phi &= \frac{1}{N_p}\int_{0}^{t}V \cos \omega t \;dt\\ 
 &= \frac{V}{\omega N_p}\sin \omega t\\ 
 &\text{Now reluctance} \\ 
 \Re &= \frac{N_p I \sin \omega t}{\frac{V}{\omega N_p} \sin \omega t}\\ 
 &= \frac{N_p^2\omega I}{V}\\
& \text{So mean radius,}\\
R&=\frac{N_p^2 \times \omega I \times \mu r^2}{2V}
\end{aligned}[/latex]

2018.explanation_text:
At [latex]G_2[/latex] load demand is 20 pu, [latex]G_2[/latex] supplies only 15 pu. Remaining supplied by [latex]G_1[/latex] through transmission line. [latex]\begin{aligned}
P_S&=\left | \frac{V_SV_R}{X_L} \right | \sin \delta \\
5&=\frac{1 \times 1}{0.1} \sin \delta \\
\delta &=30^{\circ}\\
Q_S&=\frac{V_S^2}{X_L}-\frac{V_SV_R}{X_L} \cos \delta \\
&=\frac{1^2}{0.1}-\frac{1 \times 1 }{0.1} \cos 30^{\circ}\\
&=1.34 p.u.\\
Q_R&=\left | \frac{V_SV_R}{X_L} \right | \cos \delta -\left | \frac{V_R^2}{X_L} \right | \\
5&=\frac{1 \times 1}{0.1} \cos 30^{\circ}-\frac{1^2}{0.1} \\
&=-1.34p.u.\\
Q_{loss}&+Q_S-Q_R\\
&=1.34-(-1.34)=2.68p.u.\\
\text{At }G_1: \; Q_{G1}&=Q_{load}+Q_S\\
&=5+1.34=6.34p.u.\\
\text{At }G_2: \; Q_{G2}&=Q_{load}-(-Q_R)\\
&=10-(-1.34)=11.34p.u.
\end{aligned}[/latex]

30[latex]^{\circ}[/latex], then its value (in degree) at the end of the first iteration is
2018.html: The per-unit power output of a salient-pole generator which is connected to an infinite bus, is given by the expression, [latex]P= 1.4 \sin\delta + 0.15 \sin 2 \delta[/latex], where [latex]\delta[/latex] is the load angle. Newton-Raphson method is used to calculate the value of [latex]\delta[/latex] for P = 0.8 pu. If the initial guess is 30[latex]^{\circ}[/latex], then its value (in degree) at the end of the first iteration is
2018.subject: Power Systems - Load Flow Studies
2018.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} P(\delta )&=1.4 \sin \delta +0.15 \sin 2\delta =0.8\\ &=1.4 \sin \delta +0.15 \sin 2\delta -0.8=0\\ P'(\delta )&=\frac{d}{d\delta }(P(\delta ))\\ &=1.4 \cos \delta +0.30 \cos 2\delta \text{Given, } \delta _0&=30^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex] By using Newton Raphson method for single variable, [latex]\begin{aligned} \Delta \delta &=\delta _1-\delta _0=-\frac{f(\delta _0)}{f'(\delta_0)}=-\frac{P(\delta _0)}{P'(\delta_0)}\\ &=\delta _1 -30^{\circ}=-\frac{1.4 \sin 30^{\circ}+0.15 \sin 60^{\circ} -0.8}{1.4 \cos 30^{\circ}+0.3 \cos 60^{\circ}}\\ &=\delta _1 -30^{\circ}=-0.0219 \; red =-1.26^{\circ}\\ &=\delta _1 =28.74^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
2018.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} P(\delta )&=1.4 \sin \delta +0.15 \sin 2\delta =0.8\\ &=1.4 \sin \delta +0.15 \sin 2\delta -0.8=0\\ P'(\delta )&=\frac{d}{d\delta }(P(\delta ))\\ &=1.4 \cos \delta +0.30 \cos 2\delta \text{Given, } \delta _0&=30^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
By using Newton Raphson method for single variable,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \Delta \delta &=\delta _1-\delta _0=-\frac{f(\delta _0)}{f'(\delta_0)}=-\frac{P(\delta _0)}{P'(\delta_0)}\\ &=\delta _1 -30^{\circ}=-\frac{1.4 \sin 30^{\circ}+0.15 \sin 60^{\circ} -0.8}{1.4 \cos 30^{\circ}+0.3 \cos 60^{\circ}}\\ &=\delta _1 -30^{\circ}=-0.0219 \; red =-1.26^{\circ}\\ &=\delta _1 =28.74^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]

2018.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1\\ -1 &2 &0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\\ |A-\lambda I|=0\\ \begin{bmatrix} 1-\lambda & 0& -1\\ -1& 2-\lambda & 0\\ 0 & 0 &-2-\lambda \end{bmatrix}=0\\ (1-\lambda )((2-\lambda )(-2-\lambda ))-1(0-0)=0\\ \lambda =1,2,-2\\ \text{Eigen value of A are 1,2,-2}\\ \text{Eigen value of } A^3 \text{ are 1,8,-8}\\ \text{Eigen value of } A^2 \text{ are 1,4,4}\\ \text{Eigen value of } 4A \text{ are 4,8,-8}\\ \text{Eigen value of } 5I \text{ are 5,5,5}\\ A^3-A^2-4A+5I \text{ are 1,1,1}\\ \therefore \;\; |B|=(1)(1)(1)=1 \end{aligned}[/latex]

2018.explanation_text: Given, [latex]C=\frac{\varepsilon _0A}{d}=60pF[/latex] In second case: Capacitance, [latex]\begin{aligned} C_1 &=\frac{\varepsilon _0A}{d/2} =\frac{2\varepsilon _0A}{d}\\ &= 2 \times (60 pF)=120pF\\ C_2&=\frac{2\varepsilon _0\varepsilon _rA}{d} \\ &=(2 \times 60)\varepsilon _r \;pF =120\varepsilon _r \; pF\\ C_{eq}&=\frac{C_1C_2}{C_1+C_2}=\frac{120 \times 120\varepsilon _r}{(120+120\varepsilon _r)}pF \\ &= 86\;pF \;\;(given)\\ 86&=\frac{120 \times 120\varepsilon _r}{120(1+\varepsilon _r)} \\ \frac{86}{120}&= \frac{\varepsilon _r}{1+\varepsilon _r}\\ \varepsilon _r &=\frac{86}{34}=2.53 \end{aligned}[/latex]

2018.explanation_text:
Form circuit diagram, [latex]\begin{aligned}
E_{b1} &=V-I_a(R_a+R_{se}) \\ 
 &= 200-10(1)=190V\\ 
 N_1&= 1000rpm
\end{aligned}[/latex] Load torque increased by 44%  [latex](T\propto I_a^2)[/latex] [latex]
\begin{aligned}
\therefore \; \frac{T_2}{T_1} &=\left ( \frac{I_{a2}}{I_{a1}} \right )^2 \\ 
\Rightarrow \;\; \frac{1.44T_1}{T_1} &=\left ( \frac{I_{a2}}{10} \right )^2  \\ 
 \therefore \;\; I_{a2}^2&= 144\\ 
 I_{a2}&= 12A\\ 
&\text{At same voltage,}\\
 E_{b2}&=V-I_{a2}(R_a+R_{se}) \\ 
\therefore \;\; E_{b2} &= 200-12(1)=188V\\ 
 &\text{For series motor,}\\ 
 N&\propto \frac{E_b}{\phi }\;\;(\phi \propto I_a) \\ 
 \frac{N_2}{N_1}&=\frac{E_{b2}}{E_{b1}} \times \frac{I_{a1}}{I_{a2}}\\ 
\frac{N_2}{1000} &=\frac{188}{190}\times \frac{10}{12} \\
N_2&=824.56\; \text{rpm}\\ 
&\simeq 825\; \text{rpm}
\end{aligned}[/latex]

constant at 150 V. B1 is another battery bank whose voltage is constant at 50 V. The value

The value of the inductor, L is 5 mH and the ideal switch, S is operated with a switching frequency of 5 kHz with a duty ratio of 0.4. Once the circuit has attained steady state and assuming the diode D to be ideal, the power transferred from B1 to B2 (in Watt) is ___________ (up to 2 decimal places). .
2018.subject: Power Electronics - Choppers
2018.explanation_text:
During [latex]T_{on}[/latex] the circuit behaves as, [latex]\begin{aligned} V_s&=L\frac{di}{dt} \\ di&=\frac{V_s}{L}dt \end{aligned}[/latex] Integrating on both sides, [latex]\begin{aligned} I_P&=\frac{V_s}{L}T_{on}\\ T_{on}&=\alpha T=\frac{\alpha }{f}=80 \times 10^{-6}s\\ I_P&=\frac{50}{5 \times 10^{-3}}\times (80 \times 10^{-6})\\ &=0.8A \end{aligned}[/latex] During [latex]T_{off}[/latex], it is [latex]T_{on}\leq t\leq \beta T[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned}
\text{KVL,  } V_L&=V_s-V_0 \\ 
 (V_L)_{avg}&=0 \\ 
V_sT_{on}+&(V_s-V_0)(\beta T-T_{on}) =0 \\ 
V_s\beta T &=V_0(\beta T-T_{on}) \\ 
 \frac{V_0}{V_s}&=\frac{\beta }{\beta -\alpha } \\ 
 \beta &=0.6\\
&\text{Fromt the graph of } i_L, \\
I_{L(avg)}&=\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times b \times h}{T}\\
&=\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times \beta T \times I_P}{T}\\
&=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.6 \times 0.8=0.24A\\
&\text{Power transferred to } B_2 \text{ is,}\\
P&=V_s \times (I_L)_{avg}\\
  \text{ where } I_s&=I_L\\
P&=50 \times 0.24\\
&=12W
\end{aligned}[/latex]
2018.explanation_html:
During [latex]T_{on}[/latex] the circuit behaves as,
[latex]\begin{aligned} V_s&=L\frac{di}{dt} \\ di&=\frac{V_s}{L}dt \end{aligned}[/latex]
Integrating on both sides,
[latex]\begin{aligned} I_P&=\frac{V_s}{L}T_{on}\\ T_{on}&=\alpha T=\frac{\alpha }{f}=80 \times 10^{-6}s\\ I_P&=\frac{50}{5 \times 10^{-3}}\times (80 \times 10^{-6})\\ &=0.8A \end{aligned}[/latex]

During [latex]T_{off}[/latex], it is [latex]T_{on}\leq t\leq \beta T[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{KVL, } V_L&=V_s-V_0 \\ (V_L)_{avg}&=0 \\ V_sT_{on}+&(V_s-V_0)(\beta T-T_{on}) =0 \\ V_s\beta T &=V_0(\beta T-T_{on}) \\ \frac{V_0}{V_s}&=\frac{\beta }{\beta -\alpha } \\ \beta &=0.6\\ &\text{Fromt the graph of } i_L, \\ I_{L(avg)}&=\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times b \times h}{T}\\ &=\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times \beta T \times I_P}{T}\\ &=\frac{1}{2} \times 0.6 \times 0.8=0.24A\\ &\text{Power transferred to } B_2 \text{ is,}\\ P&=V_s \times (I_L)_{avg}\\ \text{ where } I_s&=I_L\\ P&=50 \times 0.24\\ &=12W \end{aligned}[/latex]

2017-set-1.subject: Electrical Machines - Synchronous Machines
2017-set-1.explanation_text: For synchronous motor, [latex]\bar{V_t}=\bar{E_f}+j\bar{I_a}X_s [/latex] As currrent is drawn at unity power factors. Therefore, [latex] \begin{aligned} E_f \cos \delta &=V_t \\ E_f&= \frac{V_t}{\cos \delta }=\frac{6.6kV}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{1}{\cos 30^{\circ}}\\ E_f&= \frac{6.6 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}} \times 2V\\ V_t &=\frac{6.6 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \therefore \;\;P_e &=\frac{3V_{ph}E_{ph}}{X_s} \sin \delta \\ &= \frac{3 \times \frac{6.6 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{6.6 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}} \times 2 }{30} \times \sin 30^{\circ}\\ &=838.3kW \end{aligned}[/latex]

A 3-bus power system is shown in the figure below, where the diagonal elements of Y-bus matrix are [latex]Y_{11}=-j12pu[/latex], [latex]\; Y_{22}=-j15pu[/latex] and [latex]Y_{33}=-j7pu[/latex]

Given,
[latex] \begin{aligned} Y_{11} &=-j12 \; p.u. \\ Y_{22} &=-j15 \; p.u.\\ Y_{33} &=-j7 \; p.u. \\ &\text{We know that,} \\ Y_{11} &=y_{12}+y_{13}=-j12 \; p.u. \;\;...(i) \\ Y_{22} &=y_{12}+y_{23}=-j15 \; p.u. \;\;...(ii) \\ Y_{33} &=y_{13}+y_{23}=-j7 \; p.u. \;\;...(iii) \\ &\text{From eq. (i) and (ii)} \\ y_{13}-y_{23} &=j3\; p.u. \\ y_{13}+y_{23} &=-j7 \; p.u. \\ y_{13}&= -j2\; p.u.\\ y_{23}&= -j5\; p.u.\\ y_{12}&= -j10\; p.u. \end{aligned}[/latex]

2017-set-1.text: Consider the unity feedback control system shown. The value of K that results in a phase margin of the system to be [latex]30^{\circ}[/latex] is _______.
2017-set-1.html: Consider the unity feedback control system shown. The value of K that results in a phase margin of the system to be [latex]30^{\circ}[/latex] is _______.
2017-set-1.subject: Control Systems - Frequency Response Analysis
2017-set-1.explanation_text: Forward path transfer function,[latex]G(s)=\frac{Ke^{-s}}{s} [/latex] Given, Phase margin [latex]=30^{\circ} [/latex] Phase margin [latex]=180^{\circ}+\phi[/latex] [latex] 30^{\circ}=180^{\circ}+\phi [/latex] [latex]\phi =-150^{\circ} [/latex] [latex]\phi =\angle G(j\omega )_{\omega =\omega _{gc}} [/latex] [where [latex]\omega _{gc}[/latex] is gain crossover frequency ] [latex] \angle G(j\omega )=-90^{\circ}-57.3\omega ^{\circ}[/latex] At [latex] \omega =\omega _{gc}[/latex] [latex] |G(j\omega )|=1 [/latex] [latex]\frac{k \times 1}{\omega }=1 [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \omega =\omega _{gc}=K \; rad/sec.[/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\;  \angle G(j\omega )_{\omega =\omega _{gc}}=-90^{\circ}-57.3K^{\circ} [/latex] [latex]-90^{\circ}-57.3K^{\circ}=-150^{\circ} [/latex] [latex]-57.3K^{\circ}=60^{\circ} [/latex] [latex]K=\frac{60}{57.3}=1.047[/latex]
2017-set-1.explanation_html:
Forward path transfer function,[latex]G(s)=\frac{Ke^{-s}}{s} [/latex]
Given,
Phase margin [latex]=30^{\circ} [/latex]
Phase margin [latex]=180^{\circ}+\phi[/latex]
[latex] 30^{\circ}=180^{\circ}+\phi [/latex]
[latex]\phi =-150^{\circ} [/latex]
[latex]\phi =\angle G(j\omega )_{\omega =\omega _{gc}} [/latex]
[where [latex]\omega _{gc}[/latex] is gain crossover frequency ]
[latex] \angle G(j\omega )=-90^{\circ}-57.3\omega ^{\circ}[/latex]
At [latex] \omega =\omega _{gc}[/latex]
[latex] |G(j\omega )|=1 [/latex]
[latex]\frac{k \times 1}{\omega }=1 [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \omega =\omega _{gc}=K \; rad/sec.[/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\; \angle G(j\omega )_{\omega =\omega _{gc}}=-90^{\circ}-57.3K^{\circ} [/latex]
[latex]-90^{\circ}-57.3K^{\circ}=-150^{\circ} [/latex]
[latex]-57.3K^{\circ}=60^{\circ} [/latex]
[latex]K=\frac{60}{57.3}=1.047[/latex]

2017-set-1.html: Let [latex]I=c\int \int_{R}xy^{2}dxdy[/latex], where R is the region shown in the figure and [latex]c=6 \times 10^{-4}[/latex]. The value of I equals________
2017-set-1.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
2017-set-1.explanation_text:
[latex]\begin{aligned}
I&=C\int \int xy^2\; dx \; dy\\
&=C\int_{x=1}^{5}\int_{y=0}^{2x}xy^2\; dx \; dy\\
&=C\int_{1}^{5}x\left.\begin{matrix}
\left ( \frac{y^3}{3} \right )
\end{matrix}\right|_{0}^{2x}\; dx\\
&=C\int_{1}^{5}x\frac{8x^3}{3}dx\\
&=C\int_{1}^{5}8\frac{x^4}{3}dx\\
&=C\frac{8}{3}\left.\begin{matrix}
\left ( \frac{x^5}{5} \right )
\end{matrix}\right|_{1}^5\\
&=\frac{8C}{3}\left ( 5^4-\frac{1}{5} \right )\\
&=\frac{8C}{3}(625-0.2)\\
&=\frac{8}{3}(6 \times 10^{-4})(625-0.2)\\
&=0.99968
\end{aligned}[/latex]

2017-set-1.explanation_text:
The differentail equation, [latex]\begin{aligned}
(t^2-81)\frac{dy}{dt}+5+y&= \sin t\\
\frac{dy}{dt}+\frac{5t}{t^2-81}y&=\frac{\sin t }{t^2-81}\\
P&=\frac{5t}{t^2-81}\\
Q&=\frac{\sin t}{t^2-81}\\
I.F&=e^{\int \rho dt}=e^{\int \frac{5t}{t^2-81}dt}\\
&=e^{\frac{5}{2}\int \frac{2t}{t^2-81}dt}=e^{\frac{5}{2}\ln ({t^2-81})}\\
&=e^{\ln {(t^2-81)^{5/2}}}=(t^2-81)^{5/2}\\
\text{Solution is }&\\
y(t^2-81)^{5/2}&=\int \frac{\sin t}{t^2-81}(t^2-81)^{5/2}dt\\
y&=\frac{\int (\sin t)(t^2-81)^{3/2}dt}{(t^2-81)^{5/2}}+\frac{C}{(t^2-81)^{5/2}}\\
&\text{The solution exist for  } t\neq -9, t\neq +9
\end{aligned}[/latex] Only option (A) not cover 9 and -9. Hence it is correct.

The differentail equation,
[latex]\begin{aligned} (t^2-81)\frac{dy}{dt}+5+y&= \sin t\\ \frac{dy}{dt}+\frac{5t}{t^2-81}y&=\frac{\sin t }{t^2-81}\\ P&=\frac{5t}{t^2-81}\\ Q&=\frac{\sin t}{t^2-81}\\ I.F&=e^{\int \rho dt}=e^{\int \frac{5t}{t^2-81}dt}\\ &=e^{\frac{5}{2}\int \frac{2t}{t^2-81}dt}=e^{\frac{5}{2}\ln ({t^2-81})}\\ &=e^{\ln {(t^2-81)^{5/2}}}=(t^2-81)^{5/2}\\ \text{Solution is }&\\ y(t^2-81)^{5/2}&=\int \frac{\sin t}{t^2-81}(t^2-81)^{5/2}dt\\ y&=\frac{\int (\sin t)(t^2-81)^{3/2}dt}{(t^2-81)^{5/2}}+\frac{C}{(t^2-81)^{5/2}}\\ &\text{The solution exist for } t\neq -9, t\neq +9 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Only option (A) not cover 9 and -9. Hence it is correct.

at 800 RPM. The armature resistance of the generator is 0.1 [latex]\Omega[/latex]. If the speed of the generator is increased to 1000 RPM, the current in amperes supplied by the generator to the DC grid is _______.
2017-set-1.html: A separately excited DC generator supplies 150 A to a 145 V DC grid. The generator is running at 800 RPM. The armature resistance of the generator is 0.1 [latex]\Omega[/latex]. If the speed of the generator is increased to 1000 RPM, the current in amperes supplied by the generator to the DC grid is _______.
2017-set-1.subject: Electrical Machines - DC Machines
2017-set-1.explanation_text: Given, [latex]R_a=0.1\Omega[/latex] As, DC generator is connected with DC grid, the output voltage will be constant. When generator is running at 800 rpm, Generator emf, [latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a1} &=V+I_{a1}R-a \\ &= 145+150 \times 0.1\\ &= 160V \end{aligned}[/latex] When generator is running at 1000 rpm, Generator emf, [latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a2} &=E_{a1} \times \frac{N_2}{N_1}\\ &= 160 \times \frac{1000}{800}\\ &= 200V \end{aligned}[/latex] So, new armature currrent will be, [latex]\begin{aligned} I_{a2} &=\frac{E_{a2}-V}{R_a}\\ &= \frac{200-145}{0.1}\\ &= 550A \end{aligned}[/latex]
2017-set-1.explanation_html:
Given, [latex]R_a=0.1\Omega[/latex]
As, DC generator is connected with DC grid, the output voltage will be constant.
When generator is running at 800 rpm,
Generator emf,
[latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a1} &=V+I_{a1}R-a \\ &= 145+150 \times 0.1\\ &= 160V \end{aligned}[/latex]
When generator is running at 1000 rpm,
Generator emf,
[latex]\begin{aligned} E_{a2} &=E_{a1} \times \frac{N_2}{N_1}\\ &= 160 \times \frac{1000}{800}\\ &= 200V \end{aligned}[/latex]
So, new armature currrent will be,
[latex]\begin{aligned} I_{a2} &=\frac{E_{a2}-V}{R_a}\\ &= \frac{200-145}{0.1}\\ &= 550A \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex]\frac{d^{2}y}{dt^{2}}+7\frac{dy}{dt}+10y(t)=4x(t)+5\frac{dx(t)}{dt}[/latex]
Where x(t) and y(t) are the input and output respectively. The impulse response of the system is (u(t) is the unit step function)

2017-set-1.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{d^2y}{dt^2}+7\frac{dy}{dt}+10y&=4x+5\frac{dx}{dt} \\ (s^2+7s+10)Y(s)&=(4+5s)X(s) \\ \frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}&=\frac{5s+4}{s^2+7s+10} \\ \text{Impulse response}&=L^{-1}(\text{Transfer function}) \\ &=L^{-1}\frac{5s+4}{(s+2)(s+5)} \\ &=L^{-1}\left [ -\frac{2}{s+2} +\frac{7}{s+5}\right ] \\ &=-2e^{-2t}u(t)+7e^{-5t}u(t) \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} Y_{11(new)} &=-j39.9-\frac{1}{j0.05}-j0.05 \\ &=-j19.95 \\ Y_{33(new)} &=-j39.9-\frac{1}{j0.05}-j0.05 \\ &=-j19.95 \\ Y_{13(new)} &=Y_{31}=-y_{13}-\frac{1}{j0.05} \\ Y_{31(new)} &=-j20-\frac{1}{j0.05}=0 \end{aligned}[/latex] So, modified admittance matrix is, [latex]=\begin{bmatrix} -j19.95 & j20 &0 \\ j20 & -j39.9 & j20\\ 0 & j20 & -j19.95 \end{bmatrix}\;pu[/latex]

2017-set-1.explanation_text: i= 1 A Here, B at point P is [latex]B=\frac{\mu _0I}{4 \pi d}(\sin \theta _1 +\sin \theta _2)[/latex] We know for each segment of hexagon magnetic field intensity due to element length dx, [latex]dH=\frac{Idx}{4 \pi r^2}i \times u_r[/latex] where, [latex]i \times u_r=(\sin \theta)\hat{k}[/latex]....perpendicular to plane of paper [latex]\begin{aligned} H &=\int dH=\int \frac{I \sin \theta}{4 \pi r^2}(dx)\hat{k} \\ B&=\mu _0 H \\ B_p&=\frac{\mu _0I}{4 \pi d}(\cos \alpha _1+\cos \alpha _2)\hat{k} \\ d&=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} l\;\;\;...\text{where}\; l=1m\\ \alpha _1&=\alpha _2 =60^{\circ}\\ |B_p| &=\frac{\mu _0 I}{4 \pi \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} }(\cos 60^{\circ} +\cos 60^{\circ}) \\ &\text{for all six segment} \\ 6 \times |B_p| &=\frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 6 \times 1}{4 \pi \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} }(1) \\ &=\frac{12}{\sqrt{3}}\times 10^{-7}=\frac{1.20}{\sqrt{3}}\times 10^{-6}T \\ B&=0.69 \mu T \end{aligned}[/latex]

The figure shows the single line diagram of a power system with a double circuit transmission
line. The expression for electrical power is  [latex]1.5 sin\delta[/latex], where [latex]\delta[/latex] is the rotor angle. The system is operating at the stable equilibrium point with mechanical power equal to 1 pu. If one of the transmission line circuits is removed, the maximum value of [latex]\delta[/latex] as the rotor swings, is 1.221 radian. If the expression for electrical power with one transmission line circuit removed is [latex] P_{max}  sin\delta[/latex], the valueof  [latex] P_{max} [/latex], in pu is _________.

The expression for electrical power is [latex]1.5 sin\delta[/latex], where [latex]\delta[/latex] is the rotor angle. The system is operating at the stable equilibrium point with mechanical power equal to 1 pu. If one of the transmission line circuits is removed, the maximum value of [latex]\delta[/latex] as the rotor swings, is 1.221 radian. If the expression for electrical power with one transmission line circuit removed is [latex] P_{max} sin\delta[/latex], the valueof [latex] P_{max} [/latex], in pu is _________.
2017-set-1.subject: Power Systems - Power System Stability
2017-set-1.explanation_text: Using equal area criteria: [latex]A_1=A_2[/latex] [latex]\int_{\delta _0}^{\delta _c}(P_{m0}-P_{max1} \sin \delta )d\delta =\int_{\delta _c}^{\delta _2}(P_{max1} \sin \delta -P_{m0})d\delta[/latex] By solving above integration, [latex]P_{max1}=\frac{P_{m0}(\delta _2-\delta _0)}{\cos \delta _0- \cos \delta _2}[/latex] Given data: [latex]\begin{aligned} P_{m0} &=1pu \\ P_e&= 1.5 \sin (\delta _0)=P_{m0}=1pu\\ \delta _0&41.8^{\circ}=0.7295\; rad \\ \delta _2 &=1.221\; rad =96.95^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex] Substitute above values in above equation, [latex]P_{max1}=\frac{1(1.221-0.7295)}{\cos 41.8- \cos 69.95}=1.220 p.u.[/latex]
2017-set-1.explanation_html:
Using equal area criteria:
[latex]A_1=A_2[/latex]
[latex]\int_{\delta _0}^{\delta _c}(P_{m0}-P_{max1} \sin \delta )d\delta =\int_{\delta _c}^{\delta _2}(P_{max1} \sin \delta -P_{m0})d\delta[/latex]
By solving above integration,
[latex]P_{max1}=\frac{P_{m0}(\delta _2-\delta _0)}{\cos \delta _0- \cos \delta _2}[/latex]
Given data:
[latex]\begin{aligned} P_{m0} &=1pu \\ P_e&= 1.5 \sin (\delta _0)=P_{m0}=1pu\\ \delta _0&41.8^{\circ}=0.7295\; rad \\ \delta _2 &=1.221\; rad =96.95^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Substitute above values in above equation,
[latex]P_{max1}=\frac{1(1.221-0.7295)}{\cos 41.8- \cos 69.95}=1.220 p.u.[/latex]

Auxiliary winding impedance [latex]=(24.5+j12.75)\Omega[/latex] Let [latex]X_c[/latex] be the reactance of the capacitor connected in auxiliary winding [latex]
\begin{aligned}
Z_a &= (24.5+j12.75-jX_c)\Omega \\ 
X_a &=(X_c-12.75),\; R_a=24.5\Omega  \\ 
\therefore \;\; \phi _a &=\tan^{-1}\frac{X_c-12.75}{24.5}\;...(i) \\ 
 Z_m&= 12.5+j15.75\\ 
 &= 20.10\angle 51.56^{\circ}\Omega \\ 
 \phi _m&= 51.56^{\circ}
\end{aligned}[/latex] For maximum torque at starting, condition on [latex] \phi _a[/latex] and [latex]\phi _m[/latex] is given by [latex]\left [ \phi _a=\frac{90^{\circ}-\phi _m}{2} \right ][/latex] [latex]
\phi _a=\frac{90-51.56}{2}=19.22^{\circ}}\;...(ii)
[/latex] Comparing equation (i) and (ii), [latex]
\begin{aligned}
\tan(19.22^{\circ}) &=\frac{X_c-12.75}{24.5} \\ 
0.3486 &= \frac{X_c-12.75}{24.5}\\ 
X_c &=8.541+12.75 \\ 
 \text{Capacitive reactance,}& \\ 
X_c &= 21.291\Omega \\ 
 \frac{1}{2 \pi fc}&= 21.291\\ 
 \Rightarrow \;C&= \frac{1}{2\pi \times 50 \times 21.291}\\ 
 &= 149.51\mu F
\end{aligned}[/latex]

2017-set-1.text:
Consider a causal and stable LTI system with rational transfer function H(z). Whose
corresponding impulse response begins at n = 0. Furthermore, [latex]H(1)=\frac{5}{4}[/latex]. The poles of H(z) are [latex]P_{k}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}exp(j\frac{(2k-1)\pi }{4})[/latex] for k = 1,2,3,4. The zeros of H(z) are all at z = 0. Let [latex]g[n]=j^nh[n][/latex]. The value of g[8] equals ___________.
2017-set-1.html: Consider a causal and stable LTI system with rational transfer function H(z). Whose corresponding impulse response begins at n = 0. Furthermore, [latex]H(1)=\frac{5}{4}[/latex]. The poles of H(z) are [latex]P_{k}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}exp(j\frac{(2k-1)\pi }{4})[/latex] for k = 1,2,3,4. The zeros of H(z) are all at z = 0. Let [latex]g[n]=j^nh[n][/latex]. The value of g[8] equals ___________.
2017-set-1.subject: Signals and Systems - Z-Transform
2017-set-1.explanation_text:
Pole locationof H(z) are given as, [latex]\begin{aligned} z&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}e^{j(2K-1)\frac{\pi}{4}};\;\;K=1,2,3,4\\ z_1&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}e^{j\frac{\pi}{4}} =\frac{1}{2}(1+j)\\ z_2&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}e^{j\frac{3\pi}{4}} =\frac{1}{2}(-1+j)\\ z_3&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}e^{j\frac{5\pi}{4}} =\frac{1}{2}(-1-j)\\ z_4&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}e^{j\frac{7\pi}{4}} =\frac{1}{2}(1-j)\\ \text{Now,}\\ H(z)&=\frac{K\cdot z^4}{(z-z_1)(z-z_2)(z-z_3)(z-z_4)}...(i) \end{aligned}[/latex] [As h(n) is causal and it starts from n=0, so numerator will have same order as denominator is having]. by solving equation (i) [latex]\begin{aligned}
H(z)&=\frac{K\cdot z^4}{z^4+\frac{1}{4}}\;\;...(ii)\\
&\text{Given that,}\\
H(1)&=\frac{5}{4}\\
&\text{From equation (ii),}\\
H(1)&=\frac{K}{1+\frac{1}{4}}\Rightarrow \frac{5}{4}=\frac{K}{\frac{5}{4}}\\
\Rightarrow \; K&=\frac{25}{16}\\
H(z)&=\frac{\frac{25}{16}z^4}{z^4+\frac{1}{4}}\\
&\text{By using division rule,}\\
H(z)&=\frac{25}{16}\left [ 1+\frac{1}{4}z^{-4}+\frac{1}{16}z^{-8}+... \right ]\\
\text{Thus, }h(8)&=\frac{1}{16} \times \frac{25}{16}=0.097\\
&\text{it is given that,}\\
g(n)&=j^nh(n)\\
g(8)&=j^8h(8)=h(8)\\
\Rightarrow \; g(8)&=h(8)=0.097
\end{aligned}[/latex]

[As h(n) is causal and it starts from n=0, so numerator will have same order as denominator is having]. by solving equation (i)
[latex]\begin{aligned} H(z)&=\frac{K\cdot z^4}{z^4+\frac{1}{4}}\;\;...(ii)\\ &\text{Given that,}\\ H(1)&=\frac{5}{4}\\ &\text{From equation (ii),}\\ H(1)&=\frac{K}{1+\frac{1}{4}}\Rightarrow \frac{5}{4}=\frac{K}{\frac{5}{4}}\\ \Rightarrow \; K&=\frac{25}{16}\\ H(z)&=\frac{\frac{25}{16}z^4}{z^4+\frac{1}{4}}\\ &\text{By using division rule,}\\ H(z)&=\frac{25}{16}\left [ 1+\frac{1}{4}z^{-4}+\frac{1}{16}z^{-8}+... \right ]\\ \text{Thus, }h(8)&=\frac{1}{16} \times \frac{25}{16}=0.097\\ &\text{it is given that,}\\ g(n)&=j^nh(n)\\ g(8)&=j^8h(8)=h(8)\\ \Rightarrow \; g(8)&=h(8)=0.097 \end{aligned}[/latex]

2017-set-1.html: Only one of the real roots of [latex]f(x)=x^{6}-x-1[/latex] lies in the interval [latex]1\leq x\leq 2[/latex] and bisection method is used to find its value. For achieving an accuracy of 0.001, the required minimum number of iterations is ________.
2017-set-1.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Numerical Methods
2017-set-1.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} f(x)&=x^6-x-1\\ a&=1, b=2, \in =0.01=10^{-3} \end{aligned}[/latex] The minimum number of iterations by Bisection method is given by [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{|b-a|}{2^n} &\lt \in\\ \frac{2-1}{2^n} &\lt 10^{-3}\\ \frac{1}{2^n} &\lt \frac{1}{10^{-3}}\\ 2^n &\gt 10^3\\ n &\gt \frac{\ln 1000}{\ln 2}\\ n &\gt 9.96\\ n&=10 \end{aligned}[/latex]

2017-set-1.text:
Two parallel connected, three-phase, 50Hz, 11kV, star-connected synchronous machines A and
B, are operating as synchronous condensers. They together supply 50 MVAR to a 11 kV grid.
Current supplied by both the machines are equal. Synchronous reactances of machine A and
machine B are 1[latex]\Omega[/latex] and 3[latex]\Omega[/latex] respectively. Assuming the magnetic circuit to be linear, the ratio of excitation current of machine A to that of machine B is ________.

Current supplied by both the machines are equal. Synchronous reactances of machine A and machine B are 1[latex]\Omega[/latex] and 3[latex]\Omega[/latex] respectively. Assuming the magnetic circuit to be linear, the ratio of excitation current of machine A to that of machine B is ________.
2017-set-1.subject: Electrical Machines - Synchronous Machines
2017-set-1.explanation_text: Synchronous machine A: 11 kV, 50 Hz, Y connected, [latex]X_s=1\Omega[/latex] Synchronous machine B: 11 kV, 50 Hz, Y connected, [latex]X_s=3\Omega[/latex] Given both supplying only reactive power 50MVAR tp 11 kV grid equally [latex]\begin{aligned} \therefore \; Q_A &=\sqrt{3}VI_A \sin \phi =25mVAR \\ Q_B &= \sqrt{3}VI_B \sin \phi =25mVAR\\ \therefore \;\;I_A &=\frac{25 \times 10^6}{\sqrt{3} \times 11 \times 10^3}=1312.2A \\ \therefore \;\; I_B&= 1312.2A\\ E_A &= V-jI_AX_s\\ &=\frac{11 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3}}-j1312.2\angle 90 \times 1 \\ E_B &=V_jI_BX_s \\ &= =\frac{11 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3}}-j1312.2\angle 90 \times 3 \end{aligned} [/latex] Given magnetic circuit to be linear, [latex]\begin{aligned} \therefore \;\; E &\propto I_f \\ \therefore \;\; \frac{I_{f_A}}{I_{f_B}}&=\frac{E_A}{E_B} \\ E_A&=7663.05V \\ E_B &= 10287.45V \end{aligned}[/latex] Therefore, ratio of excitation current of machine A to machine B [latex] \frac{E_A}{E_B}=0.745[/latex]
2017-set-1.explanation_html:
Synchronous machine A:
11 kV, 50 Hz, Y connected, [latex]X_s=1\Omega[/latex]

Synchronous machine B:
11 kV, 50 Hz, Y connected, [latex]X_s=3\Omega[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} \therefore \; Q_A &=\sqrt{3}VI_A \sin \phi =25mVAR \\ Q_B &= \sqrt{3}VI_B \sin \phi =25mVAR\\ \therefore \;\;I_A &=\frac{25 \times 10^6}{\sqrt{3} \times 11 \times 10^3}=1312.2A \\ \therefore \;\; I_B&= 1312.2A\\ E_A &= V-jI_AX_s\\ &=\frac{11 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3}}-j1312.2\angle 90 \times 1 \\ E_B &=V_jI_BX_s \\ &= =\frac{11 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3}}-j1312.2\angle 90 \times 3 \end{aligned} [/latex]
Given magnetic circuit to be linear,

Therefore, ratio of excitation current of machine A to machine B
[latex] \frac{E_A}{E_B}=0.745[/latex]

The positive, negative and zero sequence reactances of a wye-connected synchronous generator
are 0.2 pu, 0.2 pu, and 0.1 pu, respectively. The generator is on open circuit with a terminal
voltage of 1 pu. The minimum value of the inductive reactance, in pu, required to be connected
between neutral and ground so that the fault current does not exceed 3.75 pu if a single line to
ground fault occurs at the terminals is _______ (assume fault impedance to be zero).

2017-set-1.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} Z_1&=0.2\\ Z_2&=0.2\\ Z_0&=0.1\\ V_{Th}&=1\\ I_f&=3.75\\ &\text{For LG fault,}\\ I_f&=\frac{3V_{Th}}{Z_1+Z_2+Z_0+3Z_n}\\ 3.75&=\frac{3 \times 1}{0.2+0.2+0.1+3Z_n}\\ Z_n&=0.1\;p.u. \end{aligned}[/latex]

(vehicle does not stop) and 3 minutes of red (vehicle stops). Consider that the arrival time of

(in minutes) for the vehicle at the junction is ________.
2017-set-2.html: Assume that in a traffic junction, the cycle of the traffic signal lights is 2 minutes of green (vehicle does not stop) and 3 minutes of red (vehicle stops). Consider that the arrival time of vehicles at the junction is uniformly distributed over 5 minute cycle. The expected waiting time (in minutes) for the vehicle at the junction is ________.

2017-set-2.explanation_text: [latex]t[/latex] be arrival time of vehicles of the junction is uniformaly distributed in [0,5]. Let y be the waiting time of the junction. [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Then }y&=\left\{\begin{matrix} 0 &  t \lt 2  \\ 5-t & 2\leq t \lt 5 \end{matrix}\right.\\ y\rightarrow &[0,5]\\ f(y)&=\frac{1}{5-0}=\frac{1}{5}\\ E(y)&=\int_{-\infty }^{0}y(y)dy=\int_{0}^{5}yf(y)dy\\ &=\int_{2}^{5}y\left ( \frac{1}{5} \right )dy=\frac{1}{5}\int_{2}^{5}(5-t)dt\\ &=\frac{1}{5}\left ( 5t-\frac{t^2}{2} \right )|_2^5\\ &=\frac{1}{5}\left [ \left ( 25-\frac{25}{2} \right )-\left ( 10-\frac{4}{2} \right ) \right ]\\ &=\frac{1}{5}\left ( \frac{25}{2}-8 \right )=\frac{1}{5}\frac{9}{2}=0.9 \end{aligned}[/latex]
2017-set-2.explanation_html:
[latex]t[/latex] be arrival time of vehicles of the junction is uniformaly distributed in [0,5].
Let y be the waiting time of the junction.

[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Then }y&=\left\{\begin{matrix} 0 & t \lt 2 \\ 5-t & 2\leq t \lt 5 \end{matrix}\right.\\ y\rightarrow &[0,5]\\ f(y)&=\frac{1}{5-0}=\frac{1}{5}\\ E(y)&=\int_{-\infty }^{0}y(y)dy=\int_{0}^{5}yf(y)dy\\ &=\int_{2}^{5}y\left ( \frac{1}{5} \right )dy=\frac{1}{5}\int_{2}^{5}(5-t)dt\\ &=\frac{1}{5}\left ( 5t-\frac{t^2}{2} \right )|_2^5\\ &=\frac{1}{5}\left [ \left ( 25-\frac{25}{2} \right )-\left ( 10-\frac{4}{2} \right ) \right ]\\ &=\frac{1}{5}\left ( \frac{25}{2}-8 \right )=\frac{1}{5}\frac{9}{2}=0.9 \end{aligned}[/latex]

2017-set-2.explanation_text: Given: speed regulation of generating unit is from no load to full load. Hence, the rated frequency (50 Hz) will be common for both units at no load nad will drop to lower value as loaded to full load. Let,  [latex]P_1=[/latex] Load shared by 400 MW machine [latex]P_2=[/latex] Load shred by 300 MW machine For 400 MW machine drop in frequency from no load to full load [latex]=\frac{50 \times 4}{100}=2 Hz[/latex] New frequecy of operation of 400 MW machine, [latex]f_1=50-\frac{2}{400}P_1[/latex] For 300 MW machine drop in frequency from no load to full load [latex]=\frac{50 \times 6}{100}=3 Hz[/latex] New frequecy of operation of 300 MW machine, [latex]f_2=50-\frac{3}{300}P_2[/latex] we also know, [latex]\begin{aligned} P_1+P_2&=600 \\\ (\text{Load shared }& \text{between shared units})\\ P_2&=600-P_1 \\ f_1&=f_2=f \\ (\text{Units operatio }& \text{ is in parallel})  \\ 50-\frac{2}{400}P_1 &=50-\frac{3}{300}(600-P_1) \\ \frac{P_1}{200}&=\frac{600-P_1}{100} \\ 100P_1 &=200(600-P_1) \\ P_1&=1200-2P_1\\ 3P_1&=1200\\ P_1&=400 MW \end{aligned}[/latex]

2017-set-2.explanation_text:
[latex]\begin{aligned}
 S&=250 MVA \\ 
 \cos \phi &=0.8 \\ 
K.E. &=1000MJ \\ 
 P_e&= 60MW\\ 
 \delta _0&=10^{\circ} \\ 
 t&=10\; cycles\\
&=\frac{10}{50}=0.2\; sec \\ 
 t&=5\; cycle =0.1sec \\ 
 \text{Load}&\text{ is removed,} \\ 
 P_e&=0 \\ 
 P_a&=P_m-P_e \\ 
P_m &=60MW \\ 
 M&=\frac{HS}{180f}=\frac{K.E.}{180f} \\ 
 &= \frac{1000}{180 \times 50}=0.111\\ 
 \frac{d^2 \delta }{dt^2}&=\frac{P_a}{M}=545.45 \text{ ele.degree}/s^2 \\ 
 \text{Integrating}&\text{ the above eq.} \\
\int \left ( \frac{d^2 \delta }{dt^2} \right )dt&=\int \frac{P_a}{M}dt=545.45 \times t\\
\text{Integrating}&\text{ tit once again with dt} \\
&=545.45 \times t(dt)\\
\delta &=\frac{545.45 \times t^2}{2}=2.7^{\circ}\\
\text{So, new}&\text{ value of power angle}\\
&=10^{\circ}+2.7^{\circ}=12.7^{\circ}
\end{aligned}[/latex]

2016-set-1.explanation_text: The Z-transform of [latex]\begin{aligned} \alpha ^n u(n)&\rightarrow \frac{1}{(1-\alpha Z^{-1})}\\ n\alpha ^n u(n)&\rightarrow \frac{\alpha Z^{-1}}{(1-\alpha Z^{-1})^2}\\ \frac{\alpha Z^{-1}}{(1-\alpha Z^{-1})^2}&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }n\alpha ^nZ^{-n} \end{aligned}[/latex] If we put Z=1 in above equation, we get, [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{\alpha }{(1-\alpha )^2}&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }n\alpha ^n\\ \text{Since, }\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }n\alpha ^n&=2\alpha =\frac{\alpha }{(1-\alpha )^2}\\ \text{So,}2&=\frac{1}{(1-\alpha )^2}\\ \Rightarrow \;\;\alpha &=0.29 \end{aligned}[/latex]

If we put Z=1 in above equation, we get,

Characteristic equation,
[latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex]

2016-set-1.text: Suppose [latex]x_{1}(t) \; and \;  x_{2}(t)[/latex] have the Fourier transforms as shown below. Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
2016-set-1.html:

Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
2016-set-1.subject: Signals and Systems - Fourier Transform
2016-set-1.explanation_text: By observing [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] and [latex]X_2(j \omega )[/latex], we can say that they are not conjugate symmetric. Since, the fourier transform is not conjugate symmetric the signal will not be real. So, [latex]x_1(t), x_2(t)[/latex] are not real. Now the fourier transform of [latex]x_1(t) \cdot x_2(t)[/latex] will be [latex]\frac{1}{2\pi}X_1(j \omega )*X_2(j \omega )[/latex] and by looking at [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] and [latex]X_2(j \omega )[/latex], we can say that [latex]X_1(j \omega ) *X_2(j \omega )[/latex] will be conjugate symmetric and thus [latex]x_1(t) \cdot x_2(t)[/latex] will be real. By observing [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] and [latex]X_2(j \omega )[/latex], we can say, [latex]X_2( \omega )=X_1(- \omega )\overset{IFT}{\rightarrow}x_2(t)=x_1(-t)\;\;...(i)[/latex] Now, [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] is real. Therefore, [latex]x_1(t)[/latex] will be conjugate symmetric. [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{i.e., } x_1(t)&=x_1^*(-t) \\ \downarrow t&= -t\\ x_1(-t)&= x_1^*(t)\\ \text{Now, }x_1(t)\cdot x_2(t) &= x_1(t)\cdot x_1(-t) \;\;(from \;(i))\\ &= x_1(t)\cdot x_1^*(t)\\ &= |x_1(t)|^2=\text{real function} \end{aligned}[/latex]

By observing [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] and [latex]X_2(j \omega )[/latex], we can say,
[latex]X_2( \omega )=X_1(- \omega )\overset{IFT}{\rightarrow}x_2(t)=x_1(-t)\;\;...(i)[/latex]
Now, [latex]X_1(j \omega )[/latex] is real. Therefore, [latex]x_1(t)[/latex] will be conjugate symmetric.

The output of a continuous-time, linear time-invariant system is denoted by T{x(t)} where x(t) is the input signal. A signal z(t) is called eigen-signal of the system T, when [latex]T\{z(t)\} =  \gamma z(t)[/latex],
where [latex]\gamma[/latex] is a complex number, in general, and is called an eigenvalue of T. Suppose the impulse response of the system T is real and even. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
2016-set-1.html: The output of a continuous-time, linear time-invariant system is denoted by T{x(t)} where x(t) is the input signal. A signal z(t) is called eigen-signal of the system T, when [latex]T\{z(t)\} = \gamma z(t)[/latex], where [latex]\gamma[/latex] is a complex number, in general, and is called an eigenvalue of T. Suppose the impulse response of the system T is real and even. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
2016-set-1.subject: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
2016-set-1.explanation_text: Given that impulse response is real and even, Thus [latex]H(j\omega )[/latex] will also be real and even. Since, [latex]H(j\omega )[/latex] is real and even thus, [latex]H(j\omega )=H(-j\omega )[/latex] Now, [latex]\cos (t)[/latex] is input i.e. [latex]\frac{e^{jt}+e^{-jt}}{2}[/latex] is input Output will be [latex]\frac{H(j1)e^{jt}+H(-j1)e^{-jt}}{2}=H(j1)\left ( \frac{e^{jt}+e^{-jt}}{2} \right )= H(j1) \cos (t)[/latex] If, [latex]\sin (t)[/latex] is input i.e. [latex]\frac{e^{jt}+e^{-jt}}{2}[/latex] is input Output will be [latex]\frac{H(j1)e^{jt}+H(-j1)e^{-jt}}{2}=H(j1)\left ( \frac{e^{jt}-e^{-jt}}{2j} \right )= H(j1) \sin (t)[/latex] So, [latex]\sin (t)[/latex] and [latex]\cos (t)[/latex] are eigen signal with same eigen values.
2016-set-1.explanation_html:
Given that impulse response is real and even, Thus [latex]H(j\omega )[/latex] will also be real and even.

Since, [latex]H(j\omega )[/latex] is real and even thus,
[latex]H(j\omega )=H(-j\omega )[/latex]
Now, [latex]\cos (t)[/latex] is input i.e. [latex]\frac{e^{jt}+e^{-jt}}{2}[/latex] is input
Output will be
[latex]\frac{H(j1)e^{jt}+H(-j1)e^{-jt}}{2}=H(j1)\left ( \frac{e^{jt}+e^{-jt}}{2} \right )= H(j1) \cos (t)[/latex]
If, [latex]\sin (t)[/latex] is input i.e. [latex]\frac{e^{jt}+e^{-jt}}{2}[/latex] is input
Output will be
[latex]\frac{H(j1)e^{jt}+H(-j1)e^{-jt}}{2}=H(j1)\left ( \frac{e^{jt}-e^{-jt}}{2j} \right )= H(j1) \sin (t)[/latex]
So, [latex]\sin (t)[/latex] and [latex]\cos (t)[/latex] are eigen signal with same eigen values.

2016-set-1.explanation_text: Base current, [latex]\begin{aligned} I_B&=\frac{30 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3} \times 13.8}=1255.109A\\ I_f&=4270A\\ I_{p.u.}&=\frac{4270}{1255.109}=3.402p.u.\\ I_{g1}&=\frac{E_a}{X_1+(X_2||X_0)}\\ &\text{where, }\\ X_0&=X_0+3(Z_n+Z_f)\\ X_0&=3Z_n+0.35\\ 3.402&=\frac{1.0}{0.15+\frac{0.15 \times (3Z_n+0.35)}{0.15+3Z_n+0.35}}\\ &\text{Solving the equation,}\\ Z_n&=1.07 \;p.u. \end{aligned}[/latex]

2016-set-1.text: A single-phase 400 V, 50 Hz transformer has an iron loss of 5000 W at the rated condition. When operated at 200 V, 25 Hz, the iron loss is 2000 W. When operated at 416 V, 52 Hz, the value of the hysteresis loss divided by the eddy current loss is ______.
2016-set-1.html: A single-phase 400 V, 50 Hz transformer has an iron loss of 5000 W at the rated condition. When operated at 200 V, 25 Hz, the iron loss is 2000 W. When operated at 416 V, 52 Hz, the value of the hysteresis loss divided by the eddy current loss is ______.
2016-set-1.subject: Electrical Machines - Transformers
2016-set-1.explanation_text: 400V, 50Hz transformer, [latex]P_i=5000Watt[/latex] When, 200V, 25Hz, [latex]P_i=2000 Watt[/latex] 416V, 52Hz,  [latex]\frac{P_h}{P_e}=? [/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} P_i &=P_h+P_e \\ P_h & \propto f B_m^x \\ P_e& \propto f^2B_m^2 \end{aligned}[/latex] as in the problem [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{V}{f}&=\frac{400}{50}=\frac{416}{52}=8 \\ P_h&=Af \\ P_e&=Bf^2 \end{aligned}[/latex] From given data, [latex]\begin{aligned} 2000 &=(P_{25hZ})){i} \\ &= A(25)+B(25)^2\;\;...(i)\\ 5000 &=(P_{50Hz})_i \\ &= A(50)+B(50)^2\;\;...(ii) \end{aligned}[/latex] Solving equation (i) and (ii), [latex]\begin{aligned} A &=60,\;\; B=0.8 \\ (P_h)_{52Hz}&=Af=60 \times 52 \\ &= 3120 Watt\\ (P_e)_{52Hz}&=Bf^2=0.8 \times (52)^2 \\ &= 2163.2 Watt\\ \frac{(P_h)_{52Hz}}{(P_e)_{52Hz}}&=\frac{3120}{2163.2}=1.4423 \end{aligned}[/latex]

400V, 50Hz transformer, [latex]P_i=5000Watt[/latex]
When,
200V, 25Hz,
[latex]P_i=2000 Watt[/latex]
416V, 52Hz, [latex]\frac{P_h}{P_e}=? [/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} P_i &=P_h+P_e \\ P_h & \propto f B_m^x \\ P_e& \propto f^2B_m^2 \end{aligned}[/latex]
as in the problem
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{V}{f}&=\frac{400}{50}=\frac{416}{52}=8 \\ P_h&=Af \\ P_e&=Bf^2 \end{aligned}[/latex]
From given data,
[latex]\begin{aligned} 2000 &=(P_{25hZ})){i} \\ &= A(25)+B(25)^2\;\;...(i)\\ 5000 &=(P_{50Hz})_i \\ &= A(50)+B(50)^2\;\;...(ii) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Solving equation (i) and (ii),
[latex]\begin{aligned} A &=60,\;\; B=0.8 \\ (P_h)_{52Hz}&=Af=60 \times 52 \\ &= 3120 Watt\\ (P_e)_{52Hz}&=Bf^2=0.8 \times (52)^2 \\ &= 2163.2 Watt\\ \frac{(P_h)_{52Hz}}{(P_e)_{52Hz}}&=\frac{3120}{2163.2}=1.4423 \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex]G(s)=\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)}, K\gt 0,T \gt 0[/latex]
The closed loop system will be stable if,
2016-set-2.subject: Control Systems - Concepts of Stability
2016-set-2.explanation_text: Open loop transfer function: [latex]G(s)=\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)};[/latex]  [latex] \; K \gt 0 \; [/latex] and [latex]\; t \gt 0[/latex] For closed loop system stability, characteristic equation is, [latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex] [latex] 1+\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)}\cdot 1=0[/latex] [latex] s(1+Ts)(1+2s)+K(s+1)=0 [/latex] [latex]2Ts^3+(2+T)s^2+(1+K)s+K=0 [/latex] Using Routh's criteria, For stability, [latex]K \gt 0[/latex] and  [latex] (2+T)(1+K)-2TK \gt 0 [/latex] [latex]K(2+T-2T)+(2+T) \gt 0 [/latex] or [latex] -(T-2)K+2(2+T) \gt 0 [/latex] [latex]-K \gt -\frac{(2+T)}{(T-2)}[/latex] or  [latex] K \lt \frac{T+2}{(T-2)} [/latex] Hence for stability, [latex]0 \lt K \lt \frac{T+2}{T-2}[/latex]
2016-set-2.explanation_html:
Open loop transfer function:
[latex]G(s)=\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)};[/latex] [latex] \; K \gt 0 \; [/latex] and [latex]\; t \gt 0[/latex]
For closed loop system stability, characteristic equation is,
[latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex]
[latex] 1+\frac{K(s+1)}{s(1+Ts)(1+2s)}\cdot 1=0[/latex]
[latex] s(1+Ts)(1+2s)+K(s+1)=0 [/latex]
[latex]2Ts^3+(2+T)s^2+(1+K)s+K=0 [/latex]
Using Routh's criteria,

For stability, [latex]K \gt 0[/latex]
and [latex] (2+T)(1+K)-2TK \gt 0 [/latex]
[latex]K(2+T-2T)+(2+T) \gt 0 [/latex]
or
[latex] -(T-2)K+2(2+T) \gt 0 [/latex]
[latex]-K \gt -\frac{(2+T)}{(T-2)}[/latex] or [latex] K \lt \frac{T+2}{(T-2)} [/latex]
Hence for stability,
[latex]0 \lt K \lt \frac{T+2}{T-2}[/latex]

At no load condition, a 3-phase, 50 Hz, lossless power transmission line has sending-end and
receiving-end voltages of 400 kV and 420 kV respectively. Assuming the velocity of traveling wave to be the velocity of light, the length of the line, in km, is ____________.
2016-set-2.html: At no load condition, a 3-phase, 50 Hz, lossless power transmission line has sending-end and receiving-end voltages of 400 kV and 420 kV respectively. Assuming the velocity of traveling wave to be the velocity of light, the length of the line, in km, is ____________.
2016-set-2.subject: Power Systems - Performance of Transmission Lines, Line Parameters and Corona
2016-set-2.explanation_text: At no load, [latex]\begin{aligned} V_s&=AV_R\\ 400 &=A420\\ A&=\frac{400}{420}=0.9524\\ A&=1+\frac{YZ}{2}\\ &=1+\frac{(r+j\omega L)()g+j\omega C)}{2}\\ &\text{For lossless line,}\\ r&=0,g=0\\ \text{then,}\\ A&=1-\frac{(\omega C)(\omega L)}{2}\\ \beta l&=\sqrt{\omega L\omega C}\\ A&=0.9524=1-\frac{\beta ^2l^2}{2}\\ \beta l&=0.3085\\ \beta &=\frac{0.3085}{l}\\ \frac{V}{f}&=\frac{2\pi}{\beta }\\ \frac{3 \times 10^5}{50}&=\frac{2 \pi}{\left ( \frac{0.3085}{l} \right )}\\ l&=294.52km \end{aligned}[/latex]

At no load,
[latex]\begin{aligned} V_s&=AV_R\\ 400 &=A420\\ A&=\frac{400}{420}=0.9524\\ A&=1+\frac{YZ}{2}\\ &=1+\frac{(r+j\omega L)()g+j\omega C)}{2}\\ &\text{For lossless line,}\\ r&=0,g=0\\ \text{then,}\\ A&=1-\frac{(\omega C)(\omega L)}{2}\\ \beta l&=\sqrt{\omega L\omega C}\\ A&=0.9524=1-\frac{\beta ^2l^2}{2}\\ \beta l&=0.3085\\ \beta &=\frac{0.3085}{l}\\ \frac{V}{f}&=\frac{2\pi}{\beta }\\ \frac{3 \times 10^5}{50}&=\frac{2 \pi}{\left ( \frac{0.3085}{l} \right )}\\ l&=294.52km \end{aligned}[/latex]

2016-set-2.text: The flux linkage ([latex]\lambda[/latex]) and current (i) relation for an electromagnetic system is [latex]\lambda = (\sqrt{i})/g[/latex]. When i=2A and g (air-gap length)=10cm, the magnitude of mechanical force on the moving part, in N, is ________.
2016-set-2.html: The flux linkage ([latex]\lambda[/latex]) and current (i) relation for an electromagnetic system is [latex]\lambda = (\sqrt{i})/g[/latex]. When i=2A and g (air-gap length)=10cm, the magnitude of mechanical force on the moving part, in N, is ________.
2016-set-2.subject: Electrical machines - Single Phase Induction Motors, Special Purpose Machines and Electromechanical Energy Conversion System
2016-set-2.explanation_text: Energy in magnetic system, [latex]\begin{aligned} W_f &= \int_{0}^{\lambda } i(\lambda )\; d\lambda \\ \because \;\; i &=\lambda ^2g^2 \\ W_f &= \int_{0}^{\lambda } \lambda ^2g^2 \; d\lambda \\ &=g^2\frac{\lambda ^3}{2} \end{aligned} [/latex] Now, mechanical force, [latex]\begin{aligned} F_F &=-\frac{\partial W_f (\lambda ,g)}{\partial g} \\ &=-\frac{\partial }{\partial g} \left ( \frac{g^2\lambda ^3}{3} \right )\\ &= -\frac{2}{3}\lambda ^3 g\\ \because \;\; i=2, \;g&=10cm ,\; \lambda =10\sqrt{2} \\ \text{Hence,}\;\;|F_F|&=\frac{2}{3} \times (10\sqrt{2})^3 \times 0.1\\ &=188.56N \end{aligned}[/latex]

2016-set-2.text: The gain at the breakaway point of the root locus of a unity feedback system with open loop transfer function [latex]G(s)=\frac{Ks}{(s-1)(s-4)}[/latex] is
2016-set-2.html: The gain at the breakaway point of the root locus of a unity feedback system with open loop transfer function [latex]G(s)=\frac{Ks}{(s-1)(s-4)}[/latex] is
2016-set-2.subject: Control Systems - Root Locus Techniques
2016-set-2.explanation_text: [latex]OLTS\Rightarrow G(s)=\frac{Ks}{(s-1)(s-4)}[/latex] Now, characteristic equation, [latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex] [latex] \frac{Ks}{(s-1)(s-4)}+1=0[/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \;\; Ks+(s^2-5s+4)=0 [/latex] [latex]\;\;K=-\frac{(s^2-5s+4)}{s}=\left [ s-5+\frac{4}{s} \right ][/latex] For break away point [latex]: \frac{dK}{ds}=0[/latex] [latex] \frac{dK}{ds}=-\left [ 1-0-\frac{4}{s^2} \right ]=0 [/latex] We get, [latex]s=\pm 2[/latex] Therefore valid break away point is s=2 Now gain at s=2 is K=(Product of distances from all the poles to break away point)/(Product of distances from all the zero to break away point) Gain, [latex]K=\frac{1 \times 2}{2}=1[/latex]
2016-set-2.explanation_html:
[latex]OLTS\Rightarrow G(s)=\frac{Ks}{(s-1)(s-4)}[/latex]
Now, characteristic equation,
[latex]1+G(s)H(s)=0[/latex]
[latex] \frac{Ks}{(s-1)(s-4)}+1=0[/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \;\; Ks+(s^2-5s+4)=0 [/latex]
[latex]\;\;K=-\frac{(s^2-5s+4)}{s}=\left [ s-5+\frac{4}{s} \right ][/latex]
For break away point [latex]: \frac{dK}{ds}=0[/latex]
[latex] \frac{dK}{ds}=-\left [ 1-0-\frac{4}{s^2} \right ]=0 [/latex]
We get, [latex]s=\pm 2[/latex]
Therefore valid break away point is s=2
Now gain at s=2 is
K=(Product of distances from all the poles to break away point)/(Product of distances from all the zero to break away point)
Gain, [latex]K=\frac{1 \times 2}{2}=1[/latex]

2015-set-1.text: A random variable X has probability density function f(x) as given below: [latex]f(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix} a+bx & for \; 0 \lt x \lt 1\\ 0& otherwise \end{matrix}\right.[/latex] If the expected value E[X]=2/3, then [latex]Pr[X \lt 0.5][/latex] is _____________.
2015-set-1.html:
A random variable X has probability density function f(x) as given below:

[latex]f(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix} a+bx & for \; 0 \lt x \lt 1\\ 0& otherwise \end{matrix}\right.[/latex]

If the expected value E[X]=2/3, then [latex]Pr[X \lt 0.5][/latex] is _____________.
2015-set-1.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Probability and Statistics
2015-set-1.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} f(x)&=\left\{\begin{matrix} a+bx & \text{for }0 \lt x \lt 1\\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{matrix}\right.&\\ \text{Now given }E(X)&=2/3\\ \int_{0}^{1}xf(x)dx&=\frac{2}{3}\\ \int_{0}^{1}x(a+bx)dx&=\frac{2}{3}\\ a\left ( \frac{x^2}{2} \right )_0^1+b\left ( \frac{x^3}{3} \right )_0^1&=\frac{2}{3}\\ a\left ( \frac{1}{2} \right )+b\left ( \frac{1}{3} \right )&=\frac{2}{3}\\ 3a+2b&=4\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Now, }\int_{0}^{1}f(x)dx &=1\\ (\text{total probability} & \text{ is always equal to 1})\\ \int_{0}^{1}(a+bx)dx&=\left ( ax+\frac{bx^2}{2} \right )_0^1=1\\ a+\frac{b}{2}&=1\\ 2a+b&=2\;\;...(ii)\\ \text{Now solving } & \text{ (i) and (ii), we get}\\ a&=0,b=2\\ So,\; \;f(x)&=\left\{\begin{matrix} 2x & \text{for }0 \lt x lt 1\\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{matrix}\right.&\\ \text{Now we need}&\\ P(x \lt 0.5)&=\int_{0}^{0.5}2xdx=2\left ( \frac{x^2}{2} \right )_0^{0.5}\\ &=0.5^2-0^2=0.25 \end{aligned}[/latex]
2015-set-1.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} f(x)&=\left\{\begin{matrix} a+bx & \text{for }0 \lt x \lt 1\\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{matrix}\right.&\\ \text{Now given }E(X)&=2/3\\ \int_{0}^{1}xf(x)dx&=\frac{2}{3}\\ \int_{0}^{1}x(a+bx)dx&=\frac{2}{3}\\ a\left ( \frac{x^2}{2} \right )_0^1+b\left ( \frac{x^3}{3} \right )_0^1&=\frac{2}{3}\\ a\left ( \frac{1}{2} \right )+b\left ( \frac{1}{3} \right )&=\frac{2}{3}\\ 3a+2b&=4\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Now, }\int_{0}^{1}f(x)dx &=1\\ (\text{total probability} & \text{ is always equal to 1})\\ \int_{0}^{1}(a+bx)dx&=\left ( ax+\frac{bx^2}{2} \right )_0^1=1\\ a+\frac{b}{2}&=1\\ 2a+b&=2\;\;...(ii)\\ \text{Now solving } & \text{ (i) and (ii), we get}\\ a&=0,b=2\\ So,\; \;f(x)&=\left\{\begin{matrix} 2x & \text{for }0 \lt x lt 1\\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{matrix}\right.&\\ \text{Now we need}&\\ P(x \lt 0.5)&=\int_{0}^{0.5}2xdx=2\left ( \frac{x^2}{2} \right )_0^{0.5}\\ &=0.5^2-0^2=0.25 \end{aligned}[/latex]

2015-set-1.text: If a continuous function f(x) does not have a root in the interval [a,b], then which one of the following statements is TRUE?
2015-set-1.html: If a continuous function f(x) does not have a root in the interval [a,b], then which one of the following statements is TRUE?
2015-set-1.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
2015-set-1.explanation_text: Intermediate value theorem states that if a function is continious and [latex]f(a) \cdot f(b) \lt 0[/latex], then surely there is a root in (a,b). The contrapositive of this theorem is that if a function is continious and has no root in (a,b) then surely [latex]f(a) \cdot f(b) \geq 0[/latex]. But since it is given that there is no root in the closed interval [a,b] it means [latex]f(a) \cdot f(b) \neq 0[/latex]. So surely [latex]f(a) \cdot f(b) \gt 0[/latex] which is choise(C).

2015-set-1.text: If the sum of the diagonal elements of a 2x2 matrix is -6, then the maximum possible value of determinant of the matrix is ________.
2015-set-1.html: If the sum of the diagonal elements of a 2x2 matrix is -6, then the maximum possible value of determinant of the matrix is ________.
2015-set-1.subject: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
2015-set-1.explanation_text: Consider a symmetric matrix [latex]A =\begin{bmatrix} a & b\\ b & d \end{bmatrix}[/latex] Given [latex]a+d=-6[/latex] [latex]|A|=ad-b^2[/latex] Now since [latex]b^2[/latex] is always non-negative, maximum determinant will come when [latex]b^2=0[/latex]. So we need to maximize [latex]\begin{aligned} |A|&=ad-0=ad=a \times -(6+a) \\ &= -a^2-6a\\ \frac{d|A|}{da} &=-2a-6=0 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a &=-3 \text{ is the only stationary point} \end{aligned}[/latex] Since, [latex]\left [\frac{d^2|A|}{da} \right ]_{a=-3}=-2 \lt 0[/latex], we have a maximum at [latex]a=-3[/latex]. Since [latex]a+d=-6[/latex], corresponding value of [latex]d=-3[/latex]. [latex]|A|=ad=-3 \times -3=9[/latex]
2015-set-1.explanation_html:
Consider a symmetric matrix [latex]A =\begin{bmatrix} a & b\\ b & d \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
Given [latex]a+d=-6[/latex]
[latex]|A|=ad-b^2[/latex]
Now since [latex]b^2[/latex] is always non-negative, maximum determinant will come when [latex]b^2=0[/latex].
So we need to maximize
[latex]\begin{aligned} |A|&=ad-0=ad=a \times -(6+a) \\ &= -a^2-6a\\ \frac{d|A|}{da} &=-2a-6=0 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; a &=-3 \text{ is the only stationary point} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Since, [latex]\left [\frac{d^2|A|}{da} \right ]_{a=-3}=-2 \lt 0[/latex], we have a maximum at [latex]a=-3[/latex].
Since [latex]a+d=-6[/latex], corresponding value of [latex]d=-3[/latex].
[latex]|A|=ad=-3 \times -3=9[/latex]

f_0&=\frac{1}{2T}Hz\\

y(t)&=\frac{1}{T}\int_{t-T}^{t}\sin \omega _0\tau \; d\tau\\

2015-set-1.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} R_a &= 0.1\Omega \\ V_{OC}&= 200V\\ I'_{f}&= \frac{I_f}{2}\\ \omega '&= \frac{\omega _{rated}}{2}\\ E_g&= k\phi \omega \\ E'_g&= k\frac{\phi }{2} \times \frac{\omega }{2}\\ &= \frac{200}{4}=50V\\ V&=V(\infty )-[V(\infty )-V(0)]e^{-t/T} \\ &= 50-[50-0]e^{-t/T} \\ 25&= 50[1-e^{-t/RC} ]\\ \frac{1}{2}&= 1-e^{-t/100 \times 10^{-6}}\\ e^{-t/10^{-4}}&= \frac{1}{2}\\ t&=0.693 \times 10^{-4}\\ &=69.3\mu s \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{So,} \;\; V_2&=L_2 \frac{dI_2}{dt}+\frac{MdI_1}{dt} \\ V_2&=0 \\ \text{So,} \;\; j\omega L_2I_2 &=-j\omega MI_1 \\ \text{So,} \;\; I_2&=-I_1 \frac{M}{L_2}=-\frac{4}{5}I_1 \\ \text{Now,} \;\; V_1&= L_1 \frac{dI_1}{dt}+\frac{MdI_2}{dt} \\ V_1 &=j\omega L_1I_1+j\omega MI_2 \\ V_1&=j\omega [L_1I_1+MI_2] \\ V_1&=j\omega [800mH-384mH]I_1 \\ \frac{V_1}{I_1}&=j\omega [416mH] \end{aligned}[/latex] So, equivalent inductance is [latex]416 mH.[/latex]

The voltage source [latex]V_1[/latex] is sinusoidal with frequency 50 Hz.
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{So,} \;\; V_2&=L_2 \frac{dI_2}{dt}+\frac{MdI_1}{dt} \\ V_2&=0 \\ \text{So,} \;\; j\omega L_2I_2 &=-j\omega MI_1 \\ \text{So,} \;\; I_2&=-I_1 \frac{M}{L_2}=-\frac{4}{5}I_1 \\ \text{Now,} \;\; V_1&= L_1 \frac{dI_1}{dt}+\frac{MdI_2}{dt} \\ V_1 &=j\omega L_1I_1+j\omega MI_2 \\ V_1&=j\omega [L_1I_1+MI_2] \\ V_1&=j\omega [800mH-384mH]I_1 \\ \frac{V_1}{I_1}&=j\omega [416mH] \end{aligned}[/latex]
So, equivalent inductance is [latex]416 mH.[/latex]

2015-set-1.explanation_text:
[latex]\begin{aligned}
 D^2+5D+6&=0 \\ 
D &=-1,-3 \\ 
 y(t)&=c_1e^{-2t}+c_2e^{-3t} \\ 
\text{Given,  } y(0)&=2 \\ 
\Rightarrow \; c_1+c_2 &=2\;\;...(i) \\ 
 y(1)&=-\left ( \frac{1-3e}{e^3} \right ) \\ 
\Rightarrow \;\; \frac{c_1}{e^2}+\frac{c_2}{e^3} &= -\left ( \frac{1-3e}{e^3} \right ) \\ 
\Rightarrow \;\;ec_1+c_2 &=3e-1\;\;\;...(ii) \\ 
\text{Now solving equation} &\text{ (i) and (ii), we get} \\ 
c_1=3, &c_2=-1\\ 
 \text{Substituting in  }y(t),& we get \\ 
 y(t)&=3e^{-2t}-e^{-3t}\\
\text{Now,   }\frac{dy}{dt}&=-6e^{-2t}+3e^{-3t}\\
\left ( \frac{dy}{dt} \right )_{t=0}&=-6+3=-3 
\end{aligned}[/latex]

2015-set-1.html:
Consider the economic dispatch problem for a power plant having two generating units. The fuel costs in Rs/MWh along with the generation limits for the two units are given below:

[latex]C_{1}(P_{1})=0.01{P_{1}}^2+30P_{1}+10[/latex]; [latex]100MW\leq P_{1} \leq 150MW[/latex]
[latex] C_{2}(P_{2})=0.05{P_{2}}^2+10P_{2}+10[/latex]; [latex]100MW\leq P_{2} \leq 180MW[/latex]

The incremental cost (in Rs/MWh) of the power plant when it supplies 200 MW is ______ .
2015-set-1.subject: Power Systems - Economic Power Generation and Load Dispatch
2015-set-1.explanation_text: [latex]\begin{aligned} C_1&=0.01P_1^2+30P_1+10\\ \frac{dC_1}{dP_1}&=2 \times 0.01P_1+30\\ &=0.02P_1+30\\ C_2&=0.05P_2^2+10P_2+10\\ \frac{dC-2}{dP_2}&=0.1P_2+10\\ \text{For optimum } &\text{incremental cost,}\\ \frac{dC_1}{dP_1}&=\frac{dC_2}{dP_2}\\ 0.02P_1+30&=0.1P_2+10\\ 0.02P_1-0.1P_2&=-20 \;\;...(i)\\ \text{Given, }P_1+P_2&=200 \;\;...(ii)\\ \text{Solving } & \text{equation (i) and (ii),}\\ P_2&=200, P_1=0\\ \text{But the }& \text{range of }P_1 \text{ and }P_2 \text{ are specified as}\\ 100MW \leq & P_1 \leq 150MW\\ 100MW \leq & P_2 \leq 180MW\\ \text{hence, }& P_2=200 MW \text{ is not valid}\\ \text{so, both }& P_1 \text{ and } P_2 \text{ are operating at}\\ P_1=100,P_2=100\;& \Rightarrow \; P_1+P_2=200\\ IC_1=\frac{dC_1}{dP_1}&=0.02 \times P_1+30=32 Rs/MW\\ IC_2=\frac{dC_2}{dP_2}&=0.1 \times P_2+10=20 Rs/MW \end{aligned}[/latex]

2015-set-1.explanation_text:
Let [latex]3-\phi[/latex] fault occurs at t=0 [latex]\Rightarrow \; P_e=0\text{ for }t\geq 0^+[/latex] Now, swing equation for [latex]t\geq 0^+[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned}
\frac{2H}{\omega _s}\frac{d^2\delta }{dt^2} &=P_m \\ 
 \frac{d^2\delta }{dt^2}&= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{2H}\\ 
\frac{d\delta }{dt}&= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{2H}t+C\\ 
 C=\left.\begin{matrix}
\frac{d\delta }{dt}
\end{matrix}\right| _{t=0^+}&=\omega (t=0^+)-\omega _s\\ 
 C=\omega _s-\omega _s&=0\;(\omega (t-0^+)=\omega _s) \\ 
 \frac{d\delta }{dt}&=\frac{P_m \omega _s }{2H}t \\ 
 \Rightarrow \; \delta &= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{4H}t^2+C'\\ 
 C'&= \delta |_{t=0^+}=\delta _0\\ 
\delta  &= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{4H}t^2+\delta _0\\
\text{Now in problem,}\\
\delta (t=0.02)&\\
&=\frac{1 \times 2  \times 180  \times 50 \times 0.02^2 +5^{\circ}}{4 \times 2}\\
&=5.9^{\circ}
\end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{2H}{\omega _s}\frac{d^2\delta }{dt^2} &=P_m \\ \frac{d^2\delta }{dt^2}&= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{2H}\\ \frac{d\delta }{dt}&= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{2H}t+C\\ C=\left.\begin{matrix} \frac{d\delta }{dt} \end{matrix}\right| _{t=0^+}&=\omega (t=0^+)-\omega _s\\ C=\omega _s-\omega _s&=0\;(\omega (t-0^+)=\omega _s) \\ \frac{d\delta }{dt}&=\frac{P_m \omega _s }{2H}t \\ \Rightarrow \; \delta &= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{4H}t^2+C'\\ C'&= \delta |_{t=0^+}=\delta _0\\ \delta &= \frac{P_m \omega _s }{4H}t^2+\delta _0\\ \text{Now in problem,}\\ \delta (t=0.02)&\\ &=\frac{1 \times 2 \times 180 \times 50 \times 0.02^2 +5^{\circ}}{4 \times 2}\\ &=5.9^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]

2015-set-1.text: In the signal flow diagram given in the figure, [latex]u_{1} \; and \; u_{2}[/latex] are possible inputs whereas [latex]y_{1} \; and \;  y_{2}[/latex] are possible outputs. When would the SISO system derived from this diagram be controllable and observable?
2015-set-1.html: In the signal flow diagram given in the figure, [latex]u_{1} \; and \; u_{2}[/latex] are possible inputs whereas [latex]y_{1} \; and \; y_{2}[/latex] are possible outputs. When would the SISO system derived from this diagram be controllable and observable?
2015-set-1.subject: Control Systems - State Variable Analysis
2015-set-1.explanation_text: Equations from the flow diagram,[latex]\dot{x}_1=5x_1-2x_2+u_1 [/latex] [latex]y_1=x_1 [/latex] [latex]\dot{x}_2=5x_1+x_2+u_1+u_2 [/latex] [latex]y_2=x_1-x_2 [/latex] [latex]\dot{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2\\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}x+\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \\ 1& 1 \end{bmatrix}u [/latex] [latex]y=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}x [/latex] Considering the SISO cases:[/latex] [latex] 1. \;\;u_1(input)[/latex] and [latex] y_1(output):[/latex] [latex] A\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2\\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]B\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] and  [latex] C=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]O\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} C\\ CA \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; Rank (O)=2[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;  Observable [/latex] [latex]C\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} B & AB \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &3 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \; Rank(C)\neq 2[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; non-controllable [/latex] [latex]2.\;\;u_2(input) [/latex] and  [latex] y_1(output): [/latex] [latex]A\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2\\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]B\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] and  [latex] C\triangleq \begin{bmatrix} 1 &-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]O\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; Rank (O)=2[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; Observable [/latex] [latex]C\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 0 &-2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; Rank(C)=2[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; controllable [/latex] [latex]3. \;\;u_2(input) [/latex] and [latex] y_2(output) : [/latex] [latex]Rank(O)\neq 2\Rightarrow[/latex] non-observable [latex]Rank(C) =2 \Rightarrow [/latex] controllable [latex]4. \; \; u_1 (input) [/latex] and [latex] y_2(output)[/latex]: non-observale and non-controllable.
2015-set-1.explanation_html:
Equations from the flow diagram,[latex]\dot{x}_1=5x_1-2x_2+u_1 [/latex]
[latex]y_1=x_1 [/latex]
[latex]\dot{x}_2=5x_1+x_2+u_1+u_2 [/latex]
[latex]y_2=x_1-x_2 [/latex]
[latex]\dot{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2\\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}x+\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \\ 1& 1 \end{bmatrix}u [/latex]
[latex]y=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}x [/latex]
Considering the SISO cases:[/latex]

[latex] 1. \;\;u_1(input)[/latex] and [latex] y_1(output):[/latex]
[latex] A\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2\\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]B\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] and [latex] C=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]O\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} C\\ CA \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; Rank (O)=2[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; Observable [/latex]
[latex]C\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} B & AB \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &3 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \; Rank(C)\neq 2[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; non-controllable [/latex]

[latex]2.\;\;u_2(input) [/latex] and [latex] y_1(output): [/latex]
[latex]A\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2\\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]B\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] and [latex] C\triangleq \begin{bmatrix} 1 &-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]O\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; Rank (O)=2[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; Observable [/latex]
[latex]C\triangleq\begin{bmatrix} 0 &-2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; Rank(C)=2[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; controllable [/latex]

[latex]3. \;\;u_2(input) [/latex] and [latex] y_2(output) : [/latex]
[latex]Rank(O)\neq 2\Rightarrow[/latex] non-observable
[latex]Rank(C) =2 \Rightarrow [/latex] controllable

[latex]4. \; \; u_1 (input) [/latex] and [latex] y_2(output)[/latex]:
non-observale and non-controllable.

So, [latex]I(0^+)=0[/latex] The KVL in th loop will be [latex]V=RI+L\frac{dI}{dt}[/latex] At [latex]t=0^+ [/latex] [latex]V=RI(0^+)+L\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+) [/latex] Since, [latex] I(0^+)=0 [/latex] So, [latex]\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+)=\frac{V}{L} [/latex] Now, lets differentiate the above equation So,[latex] \frac{dV}{dt}=R\frac{dI}{dt}+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2} [/latex] [latex]\;\;0=R\frac{dI}{dt}+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2} [/latex] At [latex]t=0^+[/latex] [latex] 0=R\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+)+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2}(0^+) [/latex] So, [latex] \frac{d^2I}{dt^2}(0^+)=-\frac{R}{L^2}\cdot V[/latex]
2015-set-2.explanation_html:
Initially [latex](t=0^-)[/latex] the inductor would be uncharged.
So, [latex]I(0^+)=0[/latex]
The KVL in th loop will be
[latex]V=RI+L\frac{dI}{dt}[/latex]
At [latex]t=0^+ [/latex]
[latex]V=RI(0^+)+L\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+) [/latex]
Since, [latex] I(0^+)=0 [/latex]
So, [latex]\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+)=\frac{V}{L} [/latex]
Now, lets differentiate the above equation
So,[latex] \frac{dV}{dt}=R\frac{dI}{dt}+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2} [/latex]
[latex]\;\;0=R\frac{dI}{dt}+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2} [/latex]
At [latex]t=0^+[/latex]
[latex] 0=R\frac{dI}{dt}(0^+)+L\frac{d^2I}{dt^2}(0^+) [/latex]
So, [latex] \frac{d^2I}{dt^2}(0^+)=-\frac{R}{L^2}\cdot V[/latex]

2015-set-2.explanation_text: [latex](R_{eq})_B=\frac{2.5}{a^2} [/latex] [latex](2eq)_B=\left [ \frac{2.5}{a^2}+j\omega (1 \times 10^{-3})\right ] [/latex] [latex](2eq)_A={\left [ \frac{2.5}{a^2}+j\omega (1 \times 10^{-3})\right ]}/b^2 [/latex] [latex]Z_{in}=\frac{2.5}{a^2b^2}+\frac{ j\omega 10^{-3}}{b^2}+\frac{1}{j\omega (10 \times 10^{-5})} [/latex] [latex]Z_{in}=\frac{2.5}{a^2b^2}+j\left [ \frac{5 \times 10^3 \times 10^{-3}}{b^2} -\frac{1}{5 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times10^{-6}}\right ] \;...(i) [/latex] From problem, [latex]Z_{in}=2.5 \;\;...(ii) [/latex] From equation (i) and (ii), [latex]a^2b^2=1 [/latex] [latex]\frac{5}{b^2}-\frac{1}{5 \times 10^{-2}}=0 [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; b=0.5 \text{ and } a=2[/latex]
2015-set-2.explanation_html:
[latex](R_{eq})_B=\frac{2.5}{a^2} [/latex]
[latex](2eq)_B=\left [ \frac{2.5}{a^2}+j\omega (1 \times 10^{-3})\right ] [/latex]
[latex](2eq)_A={\left [ \frac{2.5}{a^2}+j\omega (1 \times 10^{-3})\right ]}/b^2 [/latex]
[latex]Z_{in}=\frac{2.5}{a^2b^2}+\frac{ j\omega 10^{-3}}{b^2}+\frac{1}{j\omega (10 \times 10^{-5})} [/latex]
[latex]Z_{in}=\frac{2.5}{a^2b^2}+j\left [ \frac{5 \times 10^3 \times 10^{-3}}{b^2} -\frac{1}{5 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times10^{-6}}\right ] \;...(i) [/latex]
From problem,
[latex]Z_{in}=2.5 \;\;...(ii) [/latex]
From equation (i) and (ii),
[latex]a^2b^2=1 [/latex]
[latex]\frac{5}{b^2}-\frac{1}{5 \times 10^{-2}}=0 [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; b=0.5 \text{ and } a=2[/latex]

2015-set-2.text: An open loop transfer function G(s) of a system is [latex]G(s)=\frac{K}{s(s+1)(s+2)}[/latex] For a unity feedback system, the breakaway point of the root loci on the real axis occurs at,

An open loop transfer function G(s) of a system is

For a unity feedback system, the breakaway point of the root loci on the real axis occurs at,
2015-set-2.subject: Control Systems - Root Locus Techniques
2015-set-2.explanation_text: [latex]G_1(s)=\frac{k}{s(s+1)(s+2)} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\; 1+\frac{k}{s(s+1)(s+2)}=0 [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\; s(s^2+3s+2)+k=0 [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\; s^3+3s^2+2s+k=0 [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\; k=-s^3-3s^2-2s\;\;\;...(i) [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{dk}{ds}=0[/latex] [latex] \;\;\;\;\frac{dk}{ds}=-3s^2-6s-2=0[/latex] [latex] \;\;\;\;s=-0.422,-1.577[/latex] Only s=-0.422 lie on root locus. Therefore brakaway point is s=-0.42.
2015-set-2.explanation_html:
[latex]G_1(s)=\frac{k}{s(s+1)(s+2)} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; 1+\frac{k}{s(s+1)(s+2)}=0 [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; s(s^2+3s+2)+k=0 [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; s^3+3s^2+2s+k=0 [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; k=-s^3-3s^2-2s\;\;\;...(i) [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{dk}{ds}=0[/latex]
[latex] \;\;\;\;\frac{dk}{ds}=-3s^2-6s-2=0[/latex]
[latex] \;\;\;\;s=-0.422,-1.577[/latex]

Only s=-0.422 lie on root locus. Therefore brakaway point is s=-0.42.

2015-set-2.text: For the system governed by the set of equations: [latex]dx_{1}/dt=2x_{1}+x_{2}+u [/latex] [latex]dx_{2}/dt=-2x_{1}+u [/latex] [latex] y=3x_{1}[/latex] the transfer function Y(s)/U(s) is given by
2015-set-2.html:
For the system governed by the set of equations:
[latex]dx_{1}/dt=2x_{1}+x_{2}+u [/latex]
[latex]dx_{2}/dt=-2x_{1}+u [/latex]
[latex] y=3x_{1}[/latex]
the transfer function Y(s)/U(s) is given by
2015-set-2.subject: Control Systems - Mathematical Models of Physical Systems
2015-set-2.explanation_text: [latex]\frac{dx_1}{dt}=2x_1+x_2+u\;\;\;...(i) [/latex] [latex]\frac{dx_2}{dt}=-2x_1+4\;\;\;\;...(ii)[/latex] From equation (i), [latex]sx_1=2x_1+x_2+u [/latex] [latex]sx_2=-2x_1+u [/latex] [latex]x_2=\left ( -\frac{2x_1+u}{s} \right ) [/latex] [latex]sx_1=2x_1+\left ( -\frac{2x_1+u}{s} \right )+4 [/latex] [latex]sx_1-2x_1+\frac{2x_1}{s}=\frac{4}{5}+4 [/latex] [latex]x_1\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )=u\left (1+\frac{1}{s} \right ) [/latex] [latex]\frac{x_1}{4}=\frac{\left ( 1+\frac{1}{s} \right )}{\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{y}{u}=\frac{3x-1}{u}=\frac{3\left ( 1+\frac{1}{s} \right )}{\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{y}{u}=\frac{3(s+1)}{(s^2-2s+2)}[/latex]
2015-set-2.explanation_html:
[latex]\frac{dx_1}{dt}=2x_1+x_2+u\;\;\;...(i) [/latex]
[latex]\frac{dx_2}{dt}=-2x_1+4\;\;\;\;...(ii)[/latex]
From equation (i),
[latex]sx_1=2x_1+x_2+u [/latex]
[latex]sx_2=-2x_1+u [/latex]
[latex]x_2=\left ( -\frac{2x_1+u}{s} \right ) [/latex]
[latex]sx_1=2x_1+\left ( -\frac{2x_1+u}{s} \right )+4 [/latex]
[latex]sx_1-2x_1+\frac{2x_1}{s}=\frac{4}{5}+4 [/latex]
[latex]x_1\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )=u\left (1+\frac{1}{s} \right ) [/latex]
[latex]\frac{x_1}{4}=\frac{\left ( 1+\frac{1}{s} \right )}{\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{y}{u}=\frac{3x-1}{u}=\frac{3\left ( 1+\frac{1}{s} \right )}{\left ( s-2+\frac{2}{s} \right )} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\frac{y}{u}=\frac{3(s+1)}{(s^2-2s+2)}[/latex]
